"Back at the tavern, you said something while we danced."
My breath sits lodged at the top of my throat, until I feel pressure building behind my eyes. By the time I take a deep inhale, I'm on the verge of laughing hysterically at the absurdity of this encounter. Thankfully, a giggle is all that makes it through the delayed hysteria.
"I said a few things."
"You certainly did, darling." He turns from me, only to pour two fingers of whiskey into a glass, then two more into another right beside. "But when I asked you what you wanted, tell me again what you said."
My gaze is hungry as it takes him in, the solid line of his shoulders softened by the gracefulness of his movements. The coat he wears clings close to his torso, easing at the hips where the dark finery drinks in the low light of the room. Made for darkness, I think.

The alarm blared and lights flashed, bathing the dark room in a pattern of red hue. Astarion fumbled to insert a pale blue key card into the small black rectangular pod; finally slotting it into place on the third try with shaky hands. He took a few steps back as the large metal door in front of him groaned and shifted, hinges rusted and slow after decades of disuse.
The door behind him banged loudly and he inched toward the slow moving exit. ‘Come on’ He urged silently. Bright rays of daylight spilled through the cracks, blinding him momentarily. Cold air rushed through, biting at his exposed skin. There was a loud bang behind him again and he looked back just as the barricade broke away. Cazador was rushing towards him, red eyes aflame and pallid face twisted with animalistic fury. Astarion squeezed through the small opening of the exit and slipped away just as he felt a hand graze his arm.
The landscape was dreary, bathed in grey tones. The crisp wind ripped past him, carrying an undertone of death and decay with it. He wrapped his jacket around him tighter and jogged ahead, too afraid to look back.

summary:
"I was right there!" - Astarion.
Sometimes seeking out new experiences might not what you expecting. After installing a secret mod, I found myself within the Forgotten Realms, for real, fighting for my life and for those adorable companions that we meet along the way.
It is also said that a little knowledge can be a dangerous thing as events depicted within a video game aren't necessarily going to be the ones you are expecting to encounter. Starting with a heavily modded custom honour mode run might not have been the smartest idea after all. Still, I get to meet and be with the amazing people who just need a little help from a friend.
A/N ~ if you are reading this you've most likely played the game and will have a good idea as to what happens within the progression of the game.
This is an ongoing, serialised novel that seeks to cover the majority of the story.
A first person narrative which I've chosen to create, taking a journey where the parameters of the game no longer matter or are applicable. The encounters and major events of BG3 are mostly the same as you would expect yet circumstances and choices made in the story drastically alter future events and outcomes.
Enjoy

title: The Weavewalker Saga Book 7: The Drafts that Never Should Have Been Published
author: Vestagirl
summary:
Julie Dello thought the old drafts were dead.
Before the Gaelon Chronicles became a publishing phenomenon, before Faerûn and Earth learned to speak through portals and impossible phone calls, Julie had written two strange, unfinished manuscripts she never meant anyone to see: The Shattered Weave and The Fourth Path. They were too raw, too close, too wrong.
Then Zoe finds them on a bookstore display.
Marketed as “previously unpublished works” from Julie Dello, the books should be nothing more than a publishing scandal. But the pages are changing. Readers are seeing messages that were never printed. The old drafts are not fiction. They are unstable records of another living world, and every theory thread, dramatic reading, and fan reaction is strengthening the bridge between realities.
Now Julie, Gale, Astarion, Gail, Caelin, Alex, Zoe, Vincent, and the rest of the old party have to face the terrifying possibility that a story can become a doorway when enough people believe in it.
The first thread has been restored.
The fourth path is waiting.

Ireena never considered herself a crier. Even as a child, she didn’t see the value in shedding tears and refused to on principle. As she watched her mother be lowered into the ground, she stood stock still, stone-faced, with one arm gripping Ismark’s small, weeping frame. Those around her remarked in hushed whispers about what a brave face she was putting on, how strong she was.Even so, the moment she saw her mother appear on the boat, she felt the tears she’d never shed sting her eyes. She couldn’t pinpoint why, but would later realize that this was the first time she’d ever seen her mother looking at her and only her. Ireena could only stare at the woman sitting before her, mouth agape. She looked just the same as Ireena remembered her, her soft features a mirror of Ismark’s. Ireena couldn’t see herself in them at all.___
Or, Ireena gets to speak to her mother one last time. She's unsure if she deserves to.

summary:
Rowena was bought, trained, and branded to serve a powerful man who preferred his weapons sharp and obedient.
She fixed the last problem with a dagger.
But freedom proved short-lived when a mind flayer ship crashed into the Sword Coast and left a parasite burrowing behind her eye. To survive, Rowena was forced into uneasy alliances with strangers she should not trust: a silver-tongued vampire who saw far too much of himself in her violence, and a wizard whose quiet kindness hid the kind of ambition that once nearly destroyed him.
Both men carried ghosts of their own—one haunted by a master who refused to release his hold, the other by power he was never meant to wield.
Both offered something she had never known before.
Neither came without a cost.
And as the road to Baldur’s Gate grew darker, Rowena would learn that killing her master had only been the beginning.
Because some ghosts refused to stay dead.
And some of them remembered exactly how to find her.

With Lae’zel unconscious within the astral prism, and Voss similarly subdued outside, prism tucked in his pack, the two miss out on the battle against the Grand Design. Though said battle is won on the side of Faerun and its freedom, the rebelling Githyanki are left without a leader, with a freshly-hatched egg on the worst day of their lives, and a struggle between pursuing revenge or freedom for their people.
However, with every ending is a new beginning. summary:
Calypso is a Bhaalspawn, just beginning to find the tattered edges of her past as violent acts reveal her true nature to herself.
Unable to combat the dark urges that scream within her mind, struggling for a semblance of autonomy, she begins to hide more and more of herself from her new friends after spending weeks attempting to search for any shred of her past life.
And she's not the only one clawing at the seams of this fragile exterior in an attempt for control. Astarion is finding himself rather quickly at wits end with his own emotions - as they rise and fall to the beat of his favorite drow's heart, his stone cold one finds a warmth he can't quite stomach at the thought of her demise.
In an attempt to feel real and whole, Calypso leans into the fear of falling for someone new in search of being found worthy.
In an attempt to feel safe and protected, Astarion leans into the fear of losing someone new in search of the power he set out to claim.

Far from her sun-drenched adoptive home at the Rosymorn Monastery, how did Amariel Stockhold, daughter of the Dawnmaster, find herself locked away inside the chambers of the Szarr Palace?

summary:
“Do you want us to turn back?”
Flicker made a strangled scholarly sound.
“We cannot—”
Gauthak did not look away from Maeve.
“I did not ask what was convenient.”
Maeve stared toward the silver road.
For one terrible moment, she let herself imagine saying yes.
Turning Morrow around. Riding west. Leaving Vaeloris to its towers, its archives, its princess, its ghosts.
Riding back toward colder roads, black pines, and mountain passes. Toward Little Hollow, tucked high among the northern trade routes where merchants carried furs, leathers, smoked meat, and rumors between Westruun, Emon, and the far mountain holds.
Toward home.
Or what had once been close enough to deserve the word.
But villages were going silent in the north.
People were dying.
And whatever waited beneath those mountains had already marked the road with blood.
Maeve had learned many ugly things about herself over the years, but cowardice had never taken root.
Not even when she wished it would.
“No,” she said.
Gauthak watched her carefully.
Maeve nudged Morrow forward.
“We go in.”

At Enver Gortash's urging, Ophelia, The Dark Urge, has reclaimed her name when with him alone, or working with his people. As she continues working with Enver, nearly a year after the end of the events in Personify Me, her affections for him intensify as well as her platonic adoration for his closest followers, and with all of it, more love of life as a whole and also doubts of her own faith and purposes. title: Light in the Darkness
author: Sunshine_in_the_darkness
summary:
A Baldur’s Gate 3 retelling featuring new scenes, dialogue, and deep internal monologues.
He is a master of deception. He knows exactly what words are expected of him. He knows how to mold himself into whoever they desire to see.
Astarion walks a familiar path—surrounded by the same camp, facing the same deadly trials, forging the same forced alliances. But behind every charming quip spoken aloud lies a truth no one hears.
Thoughts he dares not finish. Memories he cannot wash away. And choices that grow agonizingly heavier with every step.
Especially now, when she is near. The one who sees right through his theatrical masks—and chooses to stay anyway.
Through quiet conversations in the dark, unspoken confessions, and haunting flashbacks, this story becomes more than just a chronicle of survival. It is a desperate attempt to discover who he could truly be... if he finally stops being the creature he was made to be.

tags: The Dark Urge Resists the Urge (Baldur's Gate)
summary:
Durge awakens aboard a burning nautiloid with nothing but a pounding headache, a parasite behind his eye, and fragments of a name he can barely remember.
Stripped of his memories and haunted by violent urges he cannot explain, he is forced to navigate a world that already seems to know what he is long before he does. Every answer he uncovers raises new questions. Every step forward threatens to reveal a past he may not want to remember.
Determined to become something more than the darkness inside him, Durge gradually forges his own path. What begins as a desire for revenge against those responsible for his fate eventually grows into something larger: a vow to stand beside those who have suffered, to help them confront the monsters of their past, and to ensure those monsters answer for what they have done.
Among the companions who travel beside him is Astarion, a vampire spawn who understands all too well what it means to live with unwanted hungers. What begins as companionship and mutual dependence slowly deepens into trust, attachment, and something far more difficult for either of them to ignore.

When he wakes up, he's not himself. Not that he can remember what being 'himself' even means. All he has is a pounding headache and a name, 'The Dark Urge'.
Oh, and memories of the real world and over 500 plus hours of playtime in Baldur's Gate 3.
Now he's stuck inside the game, with no idea how he got there or what the fuck is going on. And very quickly, he'll realise that the real world of Faerun is nothing like the game. Shit hurts, there's no maps, fast travel, or save scumming. And people are far more complicated than simple video game characters.
If he can keep himself alive and make it through this, perhaps there's something waiting for him in Faerun, a life he can build for himself. But the urge is just as real as everything else, and it's out for blood.
All he wants is to find his freedom before the game kills him or the urge overtakes him.

summary:
This retelling of Baldur’s Gate 3 keeps the same faces and places you know, while lingering on the moments I wanted more of: relationships that are messy, nuanced, and human; deeper interactions with the people of Faerûn; and more grounded, realistic reactions to the events of the game. The story weaves in expanded D&D lore and incorporates images captured in photo mode. Romance is present, but so is genuine love between friends and found family — building upon the foundation created by Larian Studios.

summary:
Gale Dekarios is four years old, which is a very fine age for having important thoughts about magic and sandwiches. He lives in a rather small but very cozy house in Baldur’s Gate with his mother, Morena, and a tressym named Tara, whom he had summoned all by himself on a particularly curious afternoon.
One day, when the sun sat just right in the sky, and it was warm enough to wander, Gale decided it was an excellent day for a walk. But then, further along than he usually went, Gale found a new house. It was very big, with a tall stone wall all around it. The sort of wall that said someone important lives here. He found a small opening at the bottom of the house where some bricks had fallen out.
And in that opening, there was a room below, lit by a single lamp on the ceiling. A basement. And in the middle of the basement, cross-legged and perfectly still except for his hands, sat a little elf.
This was very curious to Gale, because there were no baby elves in Baldur’s Gate.

He wasn't aware at all, that sounds like the shit that Head Mystra would tell prospective students and parents about and would never actually care about, but he nodded anyway.

So, Mr. Ancunín, I would like you to meet Mr. Dekarios at 4:30pm sharp in the lower cafeteria today. He will tell you what to do—he's got a good head on his shoulders, and you will assist him in any way he asks."

Still with his coffers now overflowing Saphir wonders how to start extracting himself from this lifestyle and how exactly someone of his background is going to make his plans for the future work. After all a foulblood no matter their breeding is still a foulblood at the end of the day. And even the most progressive cities would most likely balk at his ideas. Although...maybe...maybe this Gortash fellow could be a way of getting his hoof in the door. After all if someone of common blood can rise through the ranks at the rate he has, surely he knows something of breaking through glass ceilings.
The man in fact did not have anything helpful to share.

summary:
It all started with the Nautiloid. There was a before, certainly. Isotta had been a scholar and a storyteller—an ethnographer—but not a mage. She had traveled the whole of Faerûn, exploring and cataloguing the people who called the material plane home. Where a wizard might hoard knowledge, Isotta sought to share it. Everything around them was just one big story, after all.
There was also a magnificent wizard named Rolan who had the misfortune to be born a tiefling. He also had the misfortune to meet a bard who claimed to be a scholar, named Isotta. Despite his best efforts to evade her, she repeatedly inserted herself into his life until he finally had no choice but to tell her he loved her, in his own way, and ask her if she might love him too—because why else could someone be so insistent on meddling if not for love? And then, dear reader, she rejected him.
____
The Way of the Wanderer is my love letter to Baldur’s Gate 3 and the grumpiest wizard deserving of love.

summary:
Mez'iraejss has spent six months finding a name no text thought worth recording: Grexivane, courtier of Azzagrat's forty-sixth layer, small enough to have escaped every cataloguing hand before hers. She raises the circle and conducts the interrogation herself. She survives it by whatever margin the evening's arithmetic sees fit to allow, goes to her knees on the vault floor in the dark, and then opens her notes each morning for six days without summoning Athux.
On the sixth day, she draws his circle. He arrives already in possession of what she did not tell him, and the conversation that follows is conducted entirely across the boundary of her seal: two creatures who have spent years becoming fluent in each other, arriving at the one exchange neither of them has prepared adequate defences for. He is furious that she nearly ceased to exist in a room he was not in. She has found his fury, and his threats of correction, rather more to her preference than she intends him to discover.

Perhaps come spring, when the ice thaws, someone will find you. Preferably someone with a conscience, one that would see to the passing of information on to someone in some way. Though, the far likelier scenario is that if someone did find you, they would see the monster you had become and burn your corpse to further cleanse the lands of your abomination.
You can lie to yourself all you want – they’re not coming for you up here. There is absolutely no way in any of the realms that they could know where you were, or where you are.
Your heart feels infinitely blacker, as if it was rotting from the inside out. Like the pain from that sadistic woman in the mindflayer colony. Gods did that hurt. Far more than the gash in your shoulder, or the hole in your side.
No – this was worse. This was deep. It was all consuming. It was the void you have been living with, simultaneously overflowing and starved of everything but space. It was the precipice between existing and caving in on yourself, being sucked into the aching emptiness within your chest.
It was the true feeling of hopelessness.

Vi narrowed her eyes a fraction, mischief tugging at the corner of her mouth. “And - your real name.”
His cheeks hollowed beautifully as he sucked a breath, expression flickering with surprise, doubt, curiosity, and finally. Respect.
“Doctor Gale Dekarios,” he admitted. “And you are?”
Game. Set. Match.
“Captain Violante Calder.” She grasped his hand. “Welcome to the Eurydice.”
When his skin finally touched hers, the electricity fried every nerve. Her gaze locked to his, and for a moment, she forgot everything - the deal, the crew, the illegal cargo. Then the heat she’d desperately been ignoring finally broke through, roaring and undeniable.
Gods, he might be the most infuriating man she’d ever met. But she also wanted him biblically.

summary:
Disar Monia grows up in a wealthy merchant family in Neverwinter, where her life is carefully controlled and her future already planned. She is expected to be perfect—educated, graceful, and ready to marry someone who will benefit her family. To everyone around her, she plays the role well, but it isn’t who she truly is.
Everything becomes harder when her mother pushes her toward a match with someone who once hurt her. The more Disar resists, the clearer it becomes that her choices don’t matter. Staying means eventually giving in to a life she doesn’t want.
Looking for something real, she begins sneaking out at night. In taverns across the city, she performs music and experiences a world far removed from her own—one where no one knows her name and nothing is decided for her. It’s uncertain, but it feels like freedom.When her family finds out, the pressure only grows. Faced with losing control of her future, Disar makes a choice: she will leave, not forever, but long enough to find her own path.
After meeting Rowin, a traveler heading south toward the Well of Dragons, she joins him, stepping into the unknown for the first time.

How did she even end up in this situation?
She kept asking herself that question while washing the sweat and grime off her body after the latest fight. Not long ago, she had been disgusted by the mere idea of gutting a fish, and now she had to scrub her skin raw, trying to get rid of the stench of goblin entrails.

So once again—how had she landed in such a completely fucked-up situation?

Just yesterday she had been installing a new game, and today she was fighting monsters, searching for a cure for the worms that had taken up residence in her skull, and dealing with strange, dark urges.

Ah, and of course—having to put up with a bunch of lunatics suffering from the same tadpole-related condition.

So let’s introduce them: a zealot with a stick up her ass, a Casanova who is definitely not a vampire (he is), an ego-overinflated mage, another zealot, a walking furnace, and a famous hero making deals with devils.

And among them—Margaret, an introverted nerd with zero combat skills, who for some completely incomprehensible reason ended up as their leader.

Zadawała sobie to pytanie, zmywając z siebie pot i brud po ostatniej walce. Jeszcze niedawno brzydziła się na samą myśl o patroszeniu ryby, a teraz musiała szorować skórę, próbując pozbyć się odoru goblińskich flaków.

Following the sudden death of Lord Cazador Szarr, Lord Astarion Ancunín is the new Marquess of Mirabar. He returns at last to Baldur's Gate with siblings Dalyria and Petras after a mysterious 20-year absence, eager to establish himself as the new Marquess and find a husband for Dalyria.

Nestled in the empty New Mexican desert, a diabolical and twisted ritual has been completed.
“Cazador Szarr. His contract exchanged the gift of sanguine immortality to one,” he held up a single red claw to emphasize this, “mortal creature. The price? Seven thousand mortal souls.”
But this makes no sense to Astarion. Although he lived his life as a full elf (a rarity in 2023 America), there were limits to the mystic and magical in the real world. Surely, there were not literal devils who stalked between planes, able to be everywhere and no where at once.

title: kissing tyrannical heads
author: babysunflowerrr
summary:
When the Banite arms dealer from Baldur's Gate crosses paths with the leader of a rising cult of Bhaal. Something sharp and electrifying catches between them at once, equal parts recognition and threat. It is not love, not even the familiar comfort of lust, but a hunger that tastes like power and punishment. Two predators circling, testing, delighted by the danger.
He speaks to the part of her that has always wanted more, with honeyed promises he plants a seed of greed in her chest and waters it with forbidden possibilities, a future in which she never has to kneel unless she chooses to. In return, she teaches him what devotion looks like when it is carved into flesh and faith, until he is stripped to something primal and raw—aching to prove himself worthy of her attention.
They know what they are. Two servants of gods who do not forgive weakness, two ambitions moving in parallel until the inevitable moment they collide. Their alliance has its days numbered, but while the blade has not fallen, why pretend at virtue? Let them indulge in the kind of fun that leaves bruises, broken promises, and a smile that feels like a sin.

“You are in a cursed land, lost in the Mists, my friends. A land plagued by darkness, death, and despair that preys upon its very people.”
As she speaks, her gaze passes from Shadowheart, to Halsin, to Gale…
“You clutch onto steel and faith, but you are far from the sight of your gods. You look to nature for guidance, but it is lifeless and brittle. You weave spells with your magic, but the Arcane in this land is tainted by hungry, evil powers.”
Finally, her eyes lock onto your crimson gaze, pinning you in place.
“Know this: You cannot make demands of the Devil, for he is the Ancient. He is the Land. And you?” Madam Eva sweeps the cards from the table in a single, fluid motion, vanishing them into a puff of violet smoke.
“You… are trespassers.” A year after defeating the Netherbrain and freeing yourself from the Szarr family, a celebratory reunion with old companions is cut short. Swept up by the Mists of Ravenloft, you are whisked away to a land of undeath and ancient magic.

Gale pulled down his nightgown around his muddy thighs and said ‘My apol-’ He coughed wetly and dripping lumps of purple sprayed across his front. ‘Sorry,’ he managed. ‘None of that was very dignified. My sincerest apologies about your necklace. I know it meant a lot to you.’ He drank messily, urgently, straight from a jug.
((the necklace? The necklace?!)) Ileleste’s hands shook as he signed. ((let me look at your arm!))
‘Why?’ He wiped his beard down cleanly and precisely with an embroidered handkerchief. A drop of water ran down his chest, past the scars of the orb and soaked into his nightgown. It was still white in places, but mostly it was red, brown and yellow; stuck stiffly to his shaking knees. ‘Never better.’

title: A Burden Shared...
author: Fafnyr
tags: Other Additional Tags to Be Added
summary:
In the three-odd years that Arvak Steelhand, a simple farmer-turned adventurer, has spent on the road with the fierce hobgobliness Vestra, there’s been little lacking in excitement. They’ve clashed swords with foes beyond count and monstrosities many times their size all across Faerûn. Through thick and thin, they've been at each other’s backs to see every fight through to their bitter end.
The pair’s latest exploit has taken them to the pleasantly bucolic town of Innisvale, ridding its green countryside of a wyvern problem. Only, one unforeseen problem arises no sooner than they’ve begun indulging in their well-earned rewards—Vestra discovers she’s gone into heat. What’s worse, as its infernal ravages begin enfevering her body and mind, every salacious thought she forms keeps straying toward her human partner.
As Vestra struggles to hide away these most violent impulses from Arvak’s knowledge, even as they threaten to overthrow her senses, Arvak finds himself worrying for his dear friend; over Vestra’s odd behaviour, and his own burgeoning feelings for her. Not merely admiration, his is a deep affection he’s kept locked away in his heart for many moons…

title: Hunger of the Weave
author: Vestagirl
summary:
Hunger of the Weave is a lyrical fantasy novella adapted from a Gale Dekarios rock opera, following Gale from lonely prodigy to Mystra’s chosen, and from catastrophic failure to the first painful steps toward reclaiming himself.
Brilliant, strange, and desperate to be understood, Gale reaches for magic as if it might finally give him a place to belong. When Mystra notices him, he mistakes divine attention for love and devotion for worth. But the closer he comes to her, the more he loses sight of himself, until one forbidden act leaves him with a hunger buried in his chest and a lifetime of shame to survive.
Rooted in the emotional arc of the original songs, Hunger of the Weave is a story about magic, ambition, grooming, guilt, and the dangerous belief that love must be earned by burning brightly enough.

Before the Shadows of Amn, before Gorion's end, there was only them. When Jaheira discovers Khalid has been secretly rewriting their life through poetry—erasing every moment his stutter stole from him—she decides words are stealing her husband away. A raw, tender, and explicit exploration of love, acceptance, and living in the imperfect present.Her gentle warrior, her quiet storm, her blushing blade was rewriting their history wherever his tongue had failed him, gilding every imperfect moment in false, painless sunlight.
That third poem—the night he first tried to tell her he loved her—had lodged in her like a thorn. In Khalid’s version, the words flowed effortlessly under starlight, his body entwined with hers. In reality, he had trembled against her, mouth opening and closing, the declaration dying into frustrated silence until he hid his face in her neck. She had held him then, patient, aching for him, and whispered that she already knew.
Were it not for the struggle, his blocks and stammers wouldn’t have bothered her in the slightest. If anything, he was her reminder, as if from Silvanus himself, to slow down and listen.

summary: Ever since I played BG3, I fell in love with its story and its characters, particularly Durge and Shadowheart. Despite how great BG3 is, I do feel like there needed to be more detail regarding the Durge storyline and how other companions reacted to events regarding his story. The goal of this 'short' narrative is to explore and delve deeper into a Durge x Shadowheart romance, it isn't going to be a complete novelization of the BG3 story since that would be too time-consuming. As a result, many of the other companion characters will have a very minimal presence within my narrative. summary:
"What did you say?" the pale man asked, sounding almost breathless. He clenched his hands at his sides, digging what appeared to be very dark, sharp nails—almost claws—into his palms.
“You're beautiful," Gale repeated, rolling onto his side. His chest ached, and his vision was blurring again. If this was a vision before death, perhaps this was his mind's strange conjuring of an angel. Might as well make the most of it. "Like an angel....or a mermaid…? But those flippers are distinct…a pinniped?" he coughed weakly, his eyelids fluttering. He was rambling like an idiot.
"Not a bad last sight," Gale murmured, letting his eyelids droop. "The mind plays such tricks…" He reached out, gripping one clammy hand in his. His attempt to lace their hands together was restricted by a delicate web between each of Astarion's pale fingers. The other man's hand went rigid as stone, but he didn't pull away.
"Depths below, you're not dying, you imbecile," Astarion snapped. "Although perhaps it'd be better if you were." Those were the last words Gale heard before he slipped beneath the wave of unconsciousness.

In a 1920s Faerûn traveling freakshow, Astarion—Gentleman Geek and reluctant performer-whisperer—is tasked with fixing the newest attraction: a melancholic merman. But the creature in the tank isn't a gaff. He's Gale, tricked and cursed by a hag to live in a freshwater tank and perform for gawking crowds.
When Astarion secretly brings him pilfered salt, something deeper than duty begins to bloom between the bloodsucker and the storm-eyed merman.For one bright instant the car lit like a stage. The merman whipped around, eyes catching the storm—hazel, wild, electric—and fixed Astarion with a glare so sharp it could have drawn blood. Sun-browned shoulders. A tail the color of bruised twilight. Gills tattered along neck and ribs. The purple scar sprawling from chest to cheek.
Names are easy things to give when the other mouth cannot argue back, but this time the Gentleman Geek felt something different stir. The merman did not like being called Murray.
“Gale,” he murmured, tasting the word like brine.

summary:
Strange. Some deeper part of him, the shrewd sailor browbeaten by decades of harshly-given warnings from pirates more wizened than even himself, knew to fear the call. Knew what lay beneath the tempting balm of it. Knew what manor of creature wailed such sweet melodies through the air to lure in its next meal.
Yet his body did not care. The song plucked away irksome thoughts of his hubris and his folly, of the flash of brilliant white that sent him toppling from the main mast to the slickened deck below. He sighed into its sound, clear and bright, and crawled forward.On the other side of the rocky outcropping, he came upon the lullaby’s source. Yes, his quivering hindbrain told him. See? There it is. Your death. Even tangled up in netting as it was.  Gale, battered and burned, washes up on a beach. He's not the only one.

After vanquishing the gnolls, the group gets most of the way to the Tollhouse before someone lets off a signal firework behind them. Tav, of course, insists they backtrack, finding a tunnel that smells as though humans had recently passed through. Why though, Astarion thinks, would the men have not used the tunnel to escape?***“Whats wrong?” Tav asked, her voice distant.
Gale stepped forward, his well tailored boots kicking up dust - his robe almost trailed in the dirt, such was its length, and Astarion couldn’t help but think it would be better off being a few inches shorter.
And then the robe moved, in an unnatural way, the end flicking horizontal and dragging, as if Gale had moved off an invisible step and left it raised behind him. Or, Astarion realized with horror, as if it had gotten caught on something strung low across the pathway, that the first three had miraculously stepped over. 
His head snapped up, finally understanding - the boulder wasn’t part of the rock wall. It was placed on top of the platform, poised to crush anyone who triggered the trap that they had only missed through sheer dumb luck.

In a world of sprawling seas and distant island chains, a spirited young ranger named Zephyrine Hawthorne lives for adventure and the promise of the unknown beyond the horizon. During a quiet morning at an inn carved into a massive ancient tree near a remote port, a sudden bandit attack throws her into the path of a mysterious traveling duelist named Vesper Blackwood.

When Zephyrine invites Vesper to join her and her companions on a voyage toward the distant Prismatic Atolls, a vast archipelago filled with bustling harbor cities, hidden dangers, ancient mysteries, and vibrant island cultures, the duelist reluctantly accepts.
Together with the calm and dependable Thorne and his sharp-tongued younger sister Lyra, the group journeys across unpredictable seas and unfamiliar islands, encountering dangerous foes, strange traditions, and unexpected friendships along the way.

The Golden Goose is gone. In her absence, the Gander's shadow has swallowed the world, and the fairy tales have curdled into something dark and hungry.
Six broken souls find each other in the wreckage: Rosamund, a sleeping beauty who woke a century late with thorns growing under her skin. Zephyros Stonehammer was five years old the first time Belladonna Prideborn looked at him like he was something worth saving.
She was all moonlight, pink ribbons, and impossible blue eyes. He was a boy raised in cold stone, sharpened into a weapon before he ever learned how to be soft. For one perfect day, she made him feel warm.
Then the world took her away.
Years later, Bella arrives at Blackwater University determined to become more than the sheltered princess everyone still treats like glass. She wants freedom. Chaos. A normal college life, if such a thing can exist in Lon Laresh, the neon-drenched City of Sin.
Then Zephyros finds her again.
He is no longer the quiet boy she remembers. He is older, darker, dangerous in all the ways she should run from—and still looking at her like she is the only thing in the world he ever learned how to want.
Bella knows better than to fall into the arms of a dragon prince with a broken heart and a possessive streak carved straight into his bones.

Baldur's Gate is rebuilding, the companions are drifting back to their own lives, and Astarion is left with a victory he can't stand in the sunlight to enjoy. Elowen chooses not to move on. Instead, she walks the road with him as another traveling companion, sharing tents, watch shifts, and late-night honesty.
What follows isn't a grand prophetic quest, but a quieter, stubborn one: Elowen begins chasing half-whispers and forgotten lore about why the sun burns a vampire spawn who refused ascension. Ruins, odd priests, strange books, wrong questions in the wrong temples—little threads she calls "research" and he calls "madness," even as he continues to follow her lead.
Afterdawn is the stretch of road where nothing huge seems to happen from the outside: campfires, small jobs, detours, close calls, and two people circling something they have no words for yet. Underneath, Elowen is pulling on something old and bright and dangerous.
Eventually the thread catches and by the end, the road looks nothing like it did at the start.

The woman tilted her head. "Do you know what we just did to you?"
Astarion's eyes darted between them, perplexed by the question. What they did to him…?
That's when he noticed the Selûnite pendant around her neck. She was a cleric… had she healed him? He tried to piece together a scenario that made any sort of sense, but the details barely added up. Had these people found him? If so, why did they drag him across the city? How did they do such a thing? Why wasn't he in Harborside getting treatment? He wasn't sure exactly how severe his injuries had been, but he knew for a fact that a simple healing potion would not have done a thing to mend him back together.
"Are you… healers?" he asked.
The bearded man's mouth dropped open. "Healers—? What? No," he began to reach for him, but thought better of it and awkwardly closed his fist instead. "Astarion, it's me. Gale."
Astarion didn't recognize his name or his face in the slightest, but the way he was looking at him gave him pause.
"I… I don't…" Astarion shook his head slightly, racking his brain. "I'm sorry… Have we met before?"

And that last time it had happened, Tav had been forced to call for Meli's help, for fear they would do something irreparably stupid. As so often happened, whenever the ever changing tide of their moods escaped them and the magic flared with chaos in consequence. But they couldn't afford stupid, not right now. Not when everybody's safety depended on their decisions.
It had to be the tadpole's doing. It had to be. No need for concern now, their mind was still their own, and everything was under control. Probably.

summary:
Days don't exist in the land of shadow. With Shar's curse sinking it's cold fingers deep into the land, Vale no longer tracks the time. And yet, he is keenly aware that the hours he spends asleep are growing fewer as the visions he faces are starting to feel less like hyper-violent nightmares and more like returning memories. Staying awake is hardly a better alternative, as the ruins in this desolate land somehow feel familiar and the ever-present Dark Urge continues to whisper in his mind. Even so, he will not waver in his promise to cure his friends of their parasites nor his vow to Astarion to free him from Cazador's control forever. When it's all over, he will finally rest.
For one glorious month, Astarion had the sun. Cast back into the dark, Shar's curse is cold and maddening. Nevertheless, Astarion holds fast to his sanity, knowing what lies at the end of this journey. Every day passed is another step closer to the cure. Every day passed is a step closer to Baldur's Gate and to exacting his bloody revenge on his vampiric master. And every day, Vale proves he is true to his promise to do anything to help Astarion. summary: “Tav.” As Halsin tested the sound, she knew it was safe on the back of his throat. Her name was dead everywhere else, but what a lovely grave his tongue marked, the shroud in which it rested. "I can see how it wouldn't fit the elegant woman you are now. Nagini suits you better. A serpentine allure and a sharp, captivating presence. A name that sounds beautiful in any tongue."Her lips curved into a genuine smile, the kind that she reserved for him. "Yes, it's a graceful one," she agreed. "I like to think that my name is like a silk dress, in a way. Smooth, elegant, and comfortable to wear."Halsin grinned at the fluidity of her nonsense. He found that perhaps the most disarming, ethereal beauties in this world were also the most eccentric; it didn't make anything about her pale, but rather highlighted everything that belonged to that strange world in which the bard reigned supreme.As Halsin helps a group of adventurers, he finds his dormant heart stirring for the party’s leader, a tiefling whose charm has been crafted to perfection from her profession as a courtesan and her bardic skills, and threatens to awake feelings that have stayed unperturbed for the last century.

She nods, her eyes skimming over the lists. "Oh, I'm sorry, could you have this translated? I'm afraid my Elvish isn't quite there yet."
“Elvish? That's all plain common.” he replies, as if it's the most obvious thing in the world.
“All of it?” she repeats, incredulous.
Thiriann suppresses a sigh. She'll be in for a long night.
"Alright. And for which date do you want them delivered?”
"Oh,delivery won't be necessary. I'll have them tonight."
Thiriann's eyes widen. "Tonight?" she echoes, disbelief coloring her voice. The sheer volume of the order, coupled with the strange, almost archaic language, is overwhelming. And on top of that, the list is handwritten.
She tries to read a few of the items but can't make heads or tails of it, his handwriting, while graceful as all elven handwriting seems to be, is also nearly impossible to decipher. There's no doubt this man has a history in medicine.

title: A Life Without Fear
author: baldursghaik
summary:
“You’re already in my head constantly—what would be different?”“Everything.”
After decades spent in the solitude of his library, studying the glamour and excitement of legends like Minsc of Rashemen and Balduran, Thyneron has envied the great heroes of Faerûn as much as he looked up to them. He always longed for adventure and thrill—but was entirely unprepared to find himself locked in a strange pod inside of an even stranger nautiloid, at the onset of an adventure he never asked for.
On he and his companion’s journey to return home to Baldur’s Gate and stop the tyranny of the Absolute, Thyneron finds that the illithid tadpole he’s been infected with has changed him—he’s bolder, braver, stronger… harder, and colder. The tadpole has bettered him, but no power comes without cost.
This is the story of Baldur’s Gate III, told through the eyes of a lonely and depressed patriar who only wants to make it home safely to see his family again, through nearly any means necessary. Much creative leeway has been taken with the game’s events, so hopefully you will enjoy this journey alongside Thyneron, Gale, Lae’zel, and Astarion, as they each chase a cure for the infection that looms over them.

She stepped out from between two oaks, soft-bellied and strong-armed, with a wild mane of auburn hair that caught in the afternoon light like a flame...
To Halsin's half-conscious, wholly-frightened eyes, she looked like nature given flesh, a radiant personification of these woods made manifest. He tried to stand, some animal instinct in the back of his mind still urging him to flee, but he had no strength. When he tried to speak, only a whimper, mortifyingly small, escaped him.
The woman grinned, interest piqued at the sorry sight of him. Her eyes gleamed, wild and insatiable, but unmistakably warm. "Well," she giggled, voice as bright as the morning sun, "what a sorry little sapling I've found in my forest!"
—

Ted squints, blinded by the sunlight reflecting off the man's golden sallet.
“Well, I saved your neck yesterday, so it would only be fair if you did me this solid and let me tag along. And besides, if you happen to find yourself in trouble again, I’ll already be there to save you once more.”
His smile is almost more dazzling than the metal. Having a travelling companion would certainly be useful, the logical thing to do to avoid fighting on his own. Having a shoulder to rely on.
Looking at this character on his white horse, in golden armour and a smug-looking face (the part he can see, with dimples on his cheeks and that perfect, pearly-white, flashing grin) Ted sees not so much a loyal companion as a fame-seeker.
Ted sighs in defeat.
"We're leaving tomorrow morning, just be ready at the pier."
After all, it’s better to have someone to use as bait if the need arises.

“Would you like to change your fate?”
 
Fate? What was fate, anyway? A curse binding him to eternal suffering, waking up every morning to see that his daughter wasn’t there? Knowing that he should skip the aisle carrying his favorite vodka, but being drawn to the numbness anyway? Was fate the inevitability that his daughter would never get to grow older than him?

“Yes.”

summary:
This is how it begins:
  "Ansur! I mean you no harm! I wish only to make an offer. Hear it, this is all I ask; turn me away, strike me down, if it bears no interest to you!"
  The storm did not die, no, but it lost its fury, its warning edge, that which bade them turn back. That shadow in the sky which sparked, sometimes, with distant lightning—it descended in swooping hooks that cut the air so cleanly, so quietly, it was almost a surprise, despite his close observation, when Balduran found Ansur before him.
  He reached his hand out, bridging half the gap, supplicant, unarmed, honest.
  Ansur hesitated for only a moment. Then, with a twist and flap of his powerful wings; with a manœuvring of his muscular neck, he pressed his crest against Balduran’s palm.
  And right there, in that instant: the eye of the storm.
You think, of course, that you know how it ends, and in a way, you are correct. That is how it ends, sometimes. This time, however, Ansur sees it happen—yes, he foresees it all—just as his Balduran arrives at Moonrise Towers, underprotected, unprepared.This is the story of how they survive.

Ruby eyes, so vibrant they would strike envy into the heart of the Lady of Love herself, seem to pierce through to his very soul with a predatory gleam, and unnaturally pale lips twist into an even more wicked smirk. A spot of blood—curse the Nine Hells, that must be Gale’s—shines at the corner of its mouth, and a tongue darts out to lick it away. The flames that birthed this devil into his realm paint streaks of orange into waves of silver hair that sweep across its brow and curl around pointed ears. Gale’s heart rabbits against his ribs, and he dares not to so much as breathe as the creature saunters away from its infernal paper prison and lands ominously close to him.
“Well, hello, darling,” the creature all but purrs, “I take it you are who I have to thank for letting me out of my cage.”
For once in his life, Gale is at a loss for words.

Gale Dekarios: The Wizard of Waterdeep. Forever set in stone.
Tall. Brave. Regal.
Liar.
He was haunting her from every corner of this city. She just wanted to forget him, forget his broken promise. But it was as though trying to forget him had only given Baldur’s Gate permission to steal the only thing she had left of him: her memories.
Soon, there would be nothing left of him that belonged only to her.
Not his name. Not his face. Not even the story of his death.
OR
She had been Gale Dekarios’s wife for less than twelve hours.
And now? She would be his widow for the rest of her life.

In the brutal world of the Baldur's Games, 24 tributes are chosen to fight to the death, and only one will survive. Nisha, selected for the 79th Games, has fought to stay alive her entire life—but now she faces a challenge that may very well be her end. Her mentor, Astarion, a charismatic winner of the 69th games, trains her in a brutal strategy: win the audience's favor to secure sponsorship, but show no mercy in the arena. He urges Nisha to eliminate her rivals early, never trust anyone, and never hesitate to kill.
As the Games approach, Nisha struggles with past and present feelings for Astarion, but he seems to have forgotten her. In a world where survival means sacrificing humanity, Nisha must decide if she really can do whatever it takes to survive. Will she outlast the bloodshed, or will the Games consume her—and everything she once was? The clock is ticking, and only one will emerge alive.

Not only that, but Mystra owns him; he knows that leaving means his career and reputation.
One evening, he escapes to the pub with friends and ends up in an unguarded conversation with the bartender. Sameera is observant and easy to talk to, with a curiosity that runs deeper than small talk. What passes between them is ordinary enough to feel harmless at first.
As they continue to cross paths, that ease becomes harder to ignore. So does the fear of repeating the past.

Some stories don't begin with a birth, but with an abandonment.
Nisha was left before the gates of the Lunathion orphanage on a moonless night, wrapped in blankets too thin for the cold, with nothing but a name engraved on a blackened locket. No one knows who brought her there. No one ever asked why.
Growing up within cold walls and under judging eyes turned her silent, like a blade wrapped in velvet. The other children feared her, and for good reason. The shadows seemed to follow her. At times, they even seemed to listen.
But it wasn't in that orphanage that Nisha found herself.
It was many years later, when she met a man with a nameless gun and a past stained with blood. A man who should have been a monster, but instead taught her what it meant to choose who to be.
Amidst forgotten ruins and statues that weep gold, Nisha became something new. A restorer of what the world sought to forget. A guardian of the cracks in time.
For Nisha didn't seek to hide the past. She recomposes it.
With shadows. With patience.
With gold.

Ardghal Ferrorum has spent his adulthood living two lives - serving as a duke in the capital region of the theocratic Kahsran Everlight Dominion by day, and by night, carrying out divine orders he receives in his dreams from his not-quite guardian angel Ayan... most of them assassinations. summary: In the wild, there are rules.Predators do not hesitate.Prey do not linger.And nothing watches without reason.Nice and simple.Tav prefers simple things. Least of all why the world keeps insisting she is prey, when everything in her instincts says she is still standing.A devil watches.A parasite whispers.A blood pool beckons.And a series of choices begins to unfold in ways none of them entirely intended.

It was never supposed to be this way. It was an accident. He was only defending himself.
Astarion Ancunín's future was ripped from him the moment he killed his beloved consort, Tavarti. Fueled by grief and anguish he buried himself with the goal of sleeping until the end of the world. What better punishment for a vampire's sins than to return to the grave he was reborn in?

Shadowmagic coursed through his veins, and perhaps that was why he had been so foolishly drawn to the white-haired vampire spawn. He was, after all, only a few steps removed from undeath himself.  He had understood the pale elf’s hungers. His fears. He had recognized himself too clearly in that desperate wish to never be afraid again. And when the moment came, the shadowsorcerer had helped the vampire spawn commit an unspeakable act; to ascend beyond fear entirely.Ciaran learned too late what followed when fear was stripped away. Those who have nothing left to fear often find pleasure in becoming fear itself. When the Netherbrain fell, and smoke settled over Baldur’s Gate, Ciaran fled to a quiet existence as a sheep farmer in the Dalelands.

A Funny Story from Hell is a post-Baldur’s Gate 3 fantasy rock musical about Karlach and Wyll after the docks, after the brain, and after the choice to return to Avernus.
Karlach is alive, but survival is not the same thing as freedom. Wyll is free of Mizora’s pact, but freedom does not erase the fine print she left behind. Together, they follow a trail of infernal ledgers, stolen blueprints, dangerous old bargains, and one extremely theatrical cambion named Flo the Garrotter toward a forge buried beneath an ancient battlefield — a forge that might finally give Karlach back her future.
Along the way, they return to the House of Hope, uncover how Karlach’s sale to Zariel connects to Gortash, Mephistopheles, the Crown of Karsus, and the rise of the Absolute, and confront the devil who once thought Wyll’s soul was hers to claim.
This is a love story, a hell road trip, a musical fix-it, and a found-family tavern tale about stolen lives, broken contracts, impossible repairs, and choosing tomorrow anyway.

summary:
This book was collected by me, Kestrel of the Winds, and filed into Candlekeep in 1489 DR.
Being a travel-notebook account compiled from Maztican testimony, shipboard interviews, Chultan confusions, caravan records, and the entirely unreliable but occasionally illuminating gossip of sailors.
By Maerovyn Tathcrown, adjunct lecturer of comparative peoples at the Font of Knowledge, Waterdeep.
With marginal notes allegedly added by Volothamp Geddarm, though I deny responsibility for their accuracy.
I had seen it kicking around, with editions created and dated to the 1380's. That it was not in Candlekeep's stacks before me is a crime. While a Waterdavian account, I did not find it widely in Circles there, even though I am familiar with Tathcrown's work.I can only surmise tthat it was targeted, and some scholarship suggests that copies existed in Candlekeep before the spellfire, and was simply lost or removed.
I will not speculate, other than to hope the offending scholar beeither presently dead, or potentially dead if this book goes missing.
-Kestrel

summary:
What happens when a child of the universe meets his demise? Does everything simply... end? Is it reborn? Is it transformed, morphed or changed? And what actually means to be "changed"? Is it limited to the physical body? Or does the soul change too?
Azrael's mind works faster than his body, or his eyes, or his physicality. And his endless need to understand the universe will be what will guide him to victory and glory. But, he will have to come to terms with his own humanity, if there's any left, and understand just how complicated it is to exist in a body made by the stars and a scalpel.
A slimy parasite will show him just how little control does he actually have of his own body, mind and existence. And a charismatic vampire will show him how much control does he have.
They are both broken souls, changed and transformed into beasts that just need a little humanity to forgive themselves. And a shoulder to cry on from time to time. May the universe guide them to each other's hearts and not lose themselves in the process.

summary:
Narcissism is a funny thing, and few understand it better than those charged with preserving it across the multiverse.
This story follows the sudden fall from grace of legal consultant Pres’tly Unknown into absolute villainy, as he sinks deeper in love with his Shadow Self. An all-powerful chaotic ephemeral twin. A soul-split. He whose creators labelled ‘Asmodeus’ before the real Asmodeus assimilated himself with their shared spirit.
It starts with a ring.
In 48 hours, time stops as a mountain is destroyed, and so too is 200km of a continent.
In 1 week, the radiation from the blast mutates all who come into contact with it, and a business bearing the crest of a fallen star shines from the wreckage.
And 1 month after that, corrupted lawyer becomes Executive over the wealthiest trade empire in Eort, as his Avarice spreads and the definitions of Good and Evil become the subject of cosmic debate.
From Tiefling to Rebis to Archvile, Pres’tly is set to become Watcher of The Fourth Circle of Hells. He holds the most powerful weapons on The Material. And Gods are the target.
War is coming.
Tyranny is devotion.
It’s all downhill from here.

summary:
They claw toward love like a drowning man claws for the surface.
The exiled saint, hiding wounds she never let heal. The rebel forged in fire, burning too bright to hold. The broken predator, desperate for redemption he doesn’t believe he deserves. And the beast cloaked in shadow, trembling beneath the weight of what she’s becoming.
They bleed, break, and stumble through ruin, haunted by gods, memories, and monsters that wear familiar faces. Every step forward cuts a little deeper. Every moment of hope is just another way to hurt.
The devil thinks he owns the soul. The vampire thinks he owns the body. They are children fighting over a corpse. I am the gravity that pulls the dead stars home. I do not need a contract. I need only time. Let them struggle. Let them burn. In the end, the dark eats everything. And she is already falling.The story begins in the game, but ends in the Void. Canon is a memory. The hunger is real.
Triggers: trauma, possession, emotional manipulation, blood. Tags are your friends.

relationships: Strahd von Zarovich/Original Dungeons & Dragons Character(s)

Strahd von Zarovich Being Strahd von Zarovich
summary:
In the shadowed land of Barovia, fate is a cage forged by gods. For centuries, the Dark Powers have written the story of Strahd von Zarovich, a tale of unrequited love and eternal damnation. Its ending is carved in stone: the monster must be destroyed. Or so we thought.
This novel was written following a 2 year Curse of Strahd campaign where my character, Melantha Darkmourn, fell in love with the man who would would become the vampire Strahd. It is a profound declaration, that the moment Strahd's love became requited, the entire equation changed. He was no longer a man defined by bitterness and loss, but a man defined by hope, because she was his hope.
Melantha's journey is not just an attempt to save a man, it is a war against destiny itself. Every scene is infused with this new purpose. Her warnings are not just cautions, but desperate attempts to stop the cascade of events that leads to the monster she once knew.
This is a story about a player who loved her character so much that she tore apart the ending to give her the happily ever after she deserved. It is a testament to the idea that love is a force powerful enough to save a soul and defy the will of the gods (even if that God is your DM!)

He’s violent, volatile, stitched together by instinct and restraint. Fighting to be good. Fighting not to enjoy the killing. And failing more often than he’ll admit.
Enter Astarion smiling, sharp-eyed, with a mouth made for mockery and a bite to match. They orbit each other like blades in flight.Somehow, it works.
Sort of.
But the more Thae’ryn uncovers about who he used to be and what he’s capable of, the harder it becomes to hold back the thing inside him. The part that wants.
And if there’s one person who might see the monster and stay anyway… it’s the only man who’s just as broken.
He’s got Thae’ryn’s back.
And a dagger to it.

This has bound them together since their very first meeting, when Artemide was only fourteen.Reivier became Artemide’s guide, her friend and her mentor in the magical arts.Four years have passed, and Artemide has grown… just as their bond has grown too.
During a party, Reivier comes down with a mild cold, but that’s hardly a problem since Artemide is ready to take care of him—even by giving him a healing potion. But what if the potion he drinks turns out to be a love potion instead?Will Artemide manage to keep him out of trouble?

Yvette, a vampire spawn, has been dragged through Menzoberranzan and the underdark for the last 10 years by her vampire master, all the way to Baldur’s Gate. Stolen from her family she was hoping to finally make her way back to them when the city's resident vampire lord killed him, freeing her. Or so she thought.
“P- please- please let me go! I just want to go back home!” Yvette pleaded as Lord Szarr loomed above her with a silver blade.
“And just where might that be?”
“R- Ravens Bluff, my lord!”
This seemed to interest the lord as he narrowed his eyes slightly.
“Perhaps, if you serve loyally, I may grant you freedom.” The lord smirked darkly down at her. “However I can't just let a spawn run off without consequence. I have a reputation to uphold, it would seem I need to make an example to show what happens to those who try to invade my territory.” He grinned as he gripped the silver blade's hilt and flipped it around in his hand.

To prove herself as an acolyte of the Waterdhavian House of the Moon, the largest temple dedicated to Selûne in Faerûn, Arûna must navigate back home after being teleported to a remote forest, armed with nothing but a backpack full of provisions and her wits. title: Until You Break
author: Aerin67
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
tags: No one is getting a healthy relationship here
"I Can Fix Him" But Actually He Can Break You
The Dark Urge Resists the Urge (Baldur's Gate)
summary:
Baldur’s Gate is technically safe. The city still bleeds — and Mirin is part of the wound. She holds it together with councils, refugees, crime and politics, until there’s nothing left but duty and exhaustion. Everyone praises their hero. No one tells her to stop. No one except the man in chains.
Enver Gortash, deposed tyrant and public monster, watches her shake through visits she insists are “fine” and calls her martyrdom what it is: a slow execution in the name of goodness. When his clean, bloodless escape turns her into the city’s scapegoat, he keeps his promise. He takes her away from the knives.
In his gilded cage, Mirin finds herself cherished, fed, and carefully contained. Gortash offers what Baldur’s Gate never did: rest, brutal honesty, and devotion that feels a lot like possession. Outside, the city howls for its missing hero. Inside, the man she tried to save patiently proves his point about power and people built to break themselves for a cause.
Leaving him means returning to martyrdom. Staying means surrendering to a love that will never let her go.
---
Updated regularly. While part of a larger collection about my Durge Mirin, this can be read as a standalone series.

title: Carnations & Explanations

summary:
Gale's head did a quick tilt of curiosity as he looked over the rim of his glasses at the grand bouquet that had been delivered. It was bursting with flora—carnations, gladiolas, lisianthis, statice, hydrangeas, larkspur, and delphinium—all in varying shades of purple. It was beautiful as it sat, perfectly fanned out at all angles, in the clear vase it arrived in.
His finger ran over the delicate petal of one of the hydrangeas. "Why send a bouquet to a florist shop?"
A snort came behind him as his friend, Jen, worked on an arrangement for an upcoming wedding. He turned to see her blowing her blunt black bangs up from where forehead.
"Maybe this mystery person is running out of ideas," she said as she snipped the end off a rose.
Gale grunted in response and responded with only one word. "Perhaps."
A sigh escaped him as one hand fell on his hip and the other scratched at his beard. It truly was a perplexing situation.

title: A Dowry of Smoke

summary:
The wrong man lived.
Gale Dekarios sacrificed himself to save the world and left his true love, Rowan Ravenshade, behind to survive the aftermath- hollow, grief-stricken, and tucked away inside her uncle's manor while he sells her future to the highest bidder. She had nothing left. No companions. No allies. No one to come to her aide.
On the other side of the city, Enver Gortash is dealing with a Parliament full of potential enemies, a succession crisis he can no longer ignore, and a list of eligible bachelorette's that he finds increasingly offensive.
All except for one.
He remembers the weight of her as she fought him. The sound she made when the world almost ended before their eyes. And for the last two years, he's had to convince himself that it hasn't affected him. That he has not thought about it since.
But karma comes for those who lie to themselves.
A "political marriage." A problem solved. A wife who will almost certainly attempt to murder him at the earliest available opportunity.
Enver Gortash has survived worse.
Probably.

title: 11. Сповідь

summary:
Лист, який Кайра написав у своєму щоденнику, поки він та його товариші були в пеклі. У момент відчаю та думок про невідворотню смерть і те, що чекає на його душу після цього, він звертається до єдиної близької людини у своєму житті. Він пише цього листа, подумки звертаючись до Енн, знаючи, що може більше ніколи її не побачити, та з кожним словом все чіткіше усвідомлюючи, наскільки вона важлива для нього. Кайрі дійсно боляче від того, що вранці він сам відштовхнув її, злякавшись близькості. Побачивши, як щиро Енн про нього піклується, провівши безсонну ніч у догляді за ним після того, як він ледь не загинув та був одержимим демоном. Кайра наговорив їй жорстоких речей, боючись, що Мальксарр нашкодить їй, як тільки дізнається про його справжні почуття.
Пізніше він відправить покладе їй цього листа в якості щирого розкаяння (і будем сподіватись, що вона його пробічить).
• Енн - півельфійка, покоївка у маєтку Біскотті, з якою у Кайри закрутився швидкий і пристрасний роман, що переріс у більш глибокі почуття.

summary:
Аврора вмить втратила все: магічні здібності, родину, дім, безпеку і статус.  В очах жреців вона лишилась тою істотою, яку вони зневажали і бажали смерті, навіть не зважаючи на те, що дівчина більше не була вампіркою.Кассандра забрала сестру до себе, але вона все ще тяжко переживає зустріч зі своєю рідною сім'єю, що всі до одного виявились вампірами, яких вона заприсяглась винищувати. Їй вдалось вберегти сестру-близнючку від смерті, провівши складний ритуал, що перетворив Аврору на людину. Заради цього Кассандра пожертвувала сувоєм, яким могла б зцілити свого коханого - Марко, або навіть себе. Її мучають сумніви, чи правильно вона вчинила, тому ставиться до Аврори холодно й відсторонено.

title: Baldur’s Gate III and the Queer Politics of Monstrosity
author: LittleMonday
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary: Would you become a monster if it would save the world? This is the central conflict of Baldur’s Gate 3, a three-act epic fantasy that continues the story of the critically acclaimed series, bringing a new threat to the city of Baldur’s Gate in the form of an illithid invasion. We, the player character, find ourselves infected with an illithid parasite and must unravel the source of the parasite’s uniqueness, and its connection to the rising Cult of the Absolute before we, too, are transformed.While an epic fantasy in scope, our infection brings us into intimate proximity with the monstrous in a relationship best described as Gothic. But what exactly is the monstrous in a setting with both high fantasy and Lovecraftian creatures? And why is it so queer? To answer this, we need to frame our understanding of the monstrous through one of the most enduring monsters in literature and media: that of Frankenstein’s Creation. Scientific experimentation, body horror, paranoia, and the Gothic all merge in Shelley’s enigmatic monster. Unraveling the seams of this Creation, both its horror and humanity, will serve as the foundation to help us piece together the nature of the monstrous in Baldur’s Gate 3.So, what is a monster?

"Of course I came, my beautiful love. Of course I came," Astarion says softly. He reaches for her, his own hand radiating barely visible black rays. Halsin's eyes are glued to his fingers, following their every move. Astarion gives him a quick sideways glance. Halsin knows to resist the allure of the black aura. Still, Astarion checks, just to be sure.Something ends, something begins.

summary:
Ezra Stormwind non ha mai deciso di venire al mondo. Di conseguenza non ha mai voluto che sua madre morisse per darlo alla luce, ma la vita aveva ben altri piani per lui.
Nella piccola tribù di Illuskan delle montagne, dove ha consumato la propria esistenza per quasi trent'anni, si vocifera che sia il prossimo capo in successione al padre, un uomo buono e magnanimo. Su ciò Ezra è di un altro parere, costretto com'è ogni giorno a nascondere le ferite inferte dal genitore, che dalla morte della moglie non fa che accanirsi sul figlio.
Perciò, dopo l'ennesima inflizione di una pena immeritata da chi lo ha messo al mondo, il ragazzo mette in atto un piano a lungo elaborato: prende le poche cose che gli appartengono e si incammina nel bosco che conduce a valle, per non fare più ritorno.Ma il clima delle montagne rocciose non è come se lo aspettava. L'inverno rigido lo sorprende, così come la bufera che travolge lui e il suo cavallo.Al risveglio è circondato da monaci, di una divinità di cui non ha mai sentito parlare, in un posto sperduto tra quegli stessi monti e, che lo voglia o meno, si ritrova costretto a restare lì per un po'...

title: Dire Desires #1
author: BadElkTales
summary: Wolfspring warns travelers about the woods beyond Watcher’s Hill. About the dire wolves. About what happens to those who stray too far.Oriana goes anyway.What she encounters are not mindless beasts, but predators who watch, who choose, and who know exactly how to take what they want. Their mounting is deliberate. Their attention unsettling. Their restraint—when it comes—feels earned rather than instinctual.As Oriana pushes deeper into her research, pleasure and danger become inseparable. The wolves do not behave like a spreading curse, nor like animals bound by hunger alone. Their numbers endure. Their memories linger. And beneath every encounter is the quiet suggestion that survival here is not accidental.Dire Desires opens Oriana’s Bestiary with an intimate descent into a town built over a secret it refuses to name—and monsters who remember what they once were.This is a rewrite of the first of the original series, but now with plot and world building.

title: dungeons, dragons & dying dreams
author: ohkielohkie
fandoms: 僕のヒーローアカデミア | Boku no Hero Academia | My Hero Academia (Anime & Manga)
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Aizawa Shouta | Eraserhead/Yamada Hizashi | Present Mic
tags: Toga Himiko is Not a Villain
Dabi | Todoroki Touya is Not a Villain
summary:
Class 1-A has been through it all. A great war? Done. Traumatic childhoods? Over. Insane levels of character development over what was logically only a year but to us felt like about twenty? Finished.
You know what’s really fun? Playing pretend. Getting to be someone else, even if it’s just for a little while. Looking around your room and watching your posters peel away like tree bark, feeling your bedsheets turn to moss carpet beneath your body.
But what happens when it starts to get harder and harder to tell where real-life stops and pretend starts? When you drift off a little too far, daydream a little too hard? Everyone in this story knows what it’s like to chase a dream so far out of your head, you stumble and fall into a reality where all of it comes true.
Maybe it’s time to give this hero course some well-deserved respite (of course, not really) and show them what a real fantasy adventure looks like. Up for a game of Dungeons & Dragons, anyone?

She reached up and grabbed his arm, trying to keep her balance.“You’re sure that’s where we need to go?” she asked quietly, in Elvish. “That is no easy task.”His expression softened and he gave her a knowing look in response.“You know of this place?” He lowered his voice to match hers, as smooth as his voice was before, it was nothing compared to hearing him speak their native tongue.“Unfortunately, yes. Westeros is a realm of looming shadows and sharp, brutal honor, a fractured tapestry woven with ambition, all while the specter of long winters always crawls closer. For Alaric Mormont, formerly a modern soldier in his past life, but now the youngest son of House Mormont of Bear Island, the chessboard of court and war has, inexplicably, gained an interface.
Alaric is bound to the System, a supernatural manifestation that replicates the rules of Dungeons and Dragons adapted to the reality of A Song of Ice and Fire. Where others see mere men, Alaric sees Level, Ability Scores, Feats, and Spells that must be earned.
Calm and reserved by nature, and with a growing connection to the natural world thanks to the class the System calls Druid, Alaric must learn to balance the philosophy and mindset of his previous life with the world of savage honor in Westeros.
Winter is coming. The Grand Game of Kings and Lords has begun. And Alaric Mormont is the only player capable of manipulating reality through a safe and powerful magic called the system.

summary:
What happens when a Chaotic Evil boy becomes a Lawful Good girl?
When cheerleaders Brittany and Tiffany try to join their high school's D&D club, the DM calls them fake gamers trying to ruin the game with their liberal agenda. Club member Corbin Kelly quits that table to join a new one run by Brittany. After all, why wouldn't he prefer playing with hot chicks over sweaty dudes? When Brittany has Corbin actually write a backstory for the Chaotic Evil murderhobo rogue he always plays, he's a little taken aback, but he's willing to go along with it if it means getting to hang out with cheerleaders every week. Brittany turns out to be a way better DM than the last guy ever was—and when the group hits high level, she even decides to run the legendary Tomb of Horrors module for them. tags: Astarion is Bad at Feelings (Baldur's Gate)
It Gets Worse Before It Gets Better
summary:
Part 1 of Fear, Fate, and Fangs in which Astarion and Tav's love story begins.
This work follows the events of Baldur's Gate 3 from Astarion's POV. It is an attempt to portray Astarion as a psychological being. I'm not analyzing him or losing myself in theories (though I am relying on psychological constructs, and my beta is a psychologist), this is rather a genuine attempt to understand him emotionally. This is why I try not to sugarcoat his actions, or idolize the 'she can fix him' trope (it might happen, though, because I, too, have my blind spots, so don't be mad at me, please).
Over the course of chapters, the language will change a bit. When Astarion opens up, so does his perspective. It's very centered and narrow at the beginning but will expand over time.
However, since this is as much a love story, there will be a lot of intimacy (sexual as well as non-sexual).There will be angst, there will be fluff, and there will be romance. There will be a lot of heartbreaking drama. But since this is a story about healing, I can assure you that eventually, everything will be fine.

You'd always heard that you shouldn't let strange men into your home, even if they may be battered and bloodied in the middle of the night. Surely no good could come of it.
~~~~~~~~~~~~
“Ask nicely.” Was all he said. Your gaze snapped to meet his, your eyes wide in disbelief. You previously had no intention of taking things very far with the elf when he showed up bloody on your doorstep but you weren’t about to let the opportunity slip from your fingers now.
“Please, Astarion.” You watched as he stood and slowly stalked over to you, placing a hand on your cheek. His ruby gaze piercing into your own, wordlessly prompting you to repeat yourself. “Astarion…”

tags: no place for altruism under this roof
summary:
There was a speech. Cazador produced a detailed list of lesser and grander mishaps committed in the past months, staring each of his children down while reciting it.They were to repent and promise improvement and only then Cazador would generously forgive them.After all, they were celebrating as a family, and a family loved one-another, no matter how undeserved the love may be.
And to express how thankful they were, each spawn was to present their father with a gift.
It was nerve-wracking, each and every year.
 
Tradition dictates that each spawn is to present Cazador with an offering on the winter solstice. Navigating the mercurial temper of the master is challenging enough, but competing against desperate siblings in a game of ever-changing rules turns these family gatherings into a fearsome ordeal.

summary:
Artemide is a young elf with red hair, freckles, and a rebellious spirit. She lives in an elven village, Avallonne, on the continent of Solias, an enchanted land where the magic of Narya and Lirinen blesses only a chosen few with special powers.
Artemide and Reivier—an elf a few years older than her, who arrived in the village years ago after studying at a magical academy—are the only druids there. This has bound them together since their very first meeting, when Artemide was only fourteen.
Reivier became Artemide’s guide, her friend and her mentor in the magical arts.
Four years have passed, and Artemide has grown… just as their bond has grown too.
 
Artemide, a 17-year-old elven druid, finds herself having to turn down a slightly too-persistent suitor. It shouldn’t be a problem—if only she were able to control her powers…
What follows is a mix of chaos, cloaks ruined forever, escapes into the forest, and heartfelt conversations about true love.
This is where Artemide and Reivier’s love story officially begins.

summary:
"The shadowed sun shall wed broken dusk,The Weaves shall fray, the gods shall rust.Through strife and love, all realmspace to save—The eclipse endures, though all else may fade.
So sayeth the wise Alaundo."
---
First, there was Ves—a half-drow bard hopelessly in love with Gale Dekarios, the wizard from Waterdeep. Their bond, born of shared trials across the Sword Coast, was unbreakable. So deeply did Ves love Gale that he sacrificed everything, even his mortal life, to remain by his side.
Now, as Moonshadow, God of the Eclipse, he is Gale’s divine partner, yet feels like a shadow in the path of Gale’s relentless ambition. Ascension has become a burden, and Moonshadow longs for the simplicity of his mortal life—of simply being Ves, Gale’s lover, free of celestial duties.
A long overdue promise to revisit Faerûn stirs those old desires, making Moonshadow yearn for a life he can never reclaim.

summary: Drakon awakens to darkness, a shredded mind and the certainty that something is deeply wrong with him.There is no past to hold onto. Only fragments: a sense of familiarity with violence, a calm that should not exist, and beneath it all, something deeper—an instinct that does not speak, but presses from within. His thoughts are precise, until something shifts.Violence comes without warning. A Dark Urge that beckons his knife-hand towards slaughter. And what frightens him is not the wish to act, but any lack of control. Killing should have a purpose, a proper reason. This Dark Urge does not control him. Not yet. But it is always there, threading through thought and action, testing the boundaries of his will.However, if there is one thing Drakon understands—it is this: [Nothing within him will rule him.]Not instinct; not past; Not whatever waits at the edge of his thoughts.If there is a will behind his creation, it will not be the final one.Drakon is the master of himself. Of that, he is sure.

summary:
Book 1 of the Threads of Fate Series
Avelyn Thornecast should have lived and died as a noblewoman of the Midnight Vale. Instead, she wakes on a cold stone floor—bruised, broken, and finally done being obedient. Her desperate escape from the husband who nearly killed her ends beneath moonlight and river water, only to be interrupted by something far stranger: a beam of impossible violet light tearing open the sky as a mind flayer ship drags her into the heavens.
She survives.Against every intention he had for her—she survives.
Now stranded far from the life she fled, Avelyn is thrown into the dangerous chaos surrounding Baldur’s Gate. With a parasite writhing behind her eyes and a mysterious artifact somehow keeping her alive, survival means forming alliances with people just as damaged as she is.
Among them is Astarion—a sharp-tongued, dangerously charming vampire spawn whose easy smile hides centuries of cruelty and control. Their tempers spark. Their scars mirror one another in ways neither of them wants to admit.
Trust is dangerous.But the road ahead may demand it.
