While on their way to Baldur's Gate, Rolan and his siblings have to settle in Emerald Grove, as the lands are overrun with goblins and mysterious cultists. It is here that he meets a peculiar drow, and the story of their unlikely relationship starts to unfold.---------------------------------------------------------------------------I always wondered how Rolan's story would unravel if a player was able to spend more time with him and romance him. summary: This is a work of original fiction inspired by a homebrewed D&D universe, called Lysendyr, where a powerful magic based on a rainbow substance called Irridescence, or Descynce, can be used in a variety of ways. We can secure the artifact and everything, certainly, but the specific techniques required to bend it to our purpose are... beyond us."

summary:
Author's note:There comes a point, if you write long enough, when the lines between yourself and the story begin to blur.I made the paladin to be everything I wished I was: brave without hesitation, loyal without apology, loving without fear. For years, I thought he was better than me, stronger, cleaner, untouched by the doubts that haunted the boy behind the pen.But stories have a way of bleeding.Six of them—paladin, cleric, ranger, rogue, mage, bard stood together, just as I always imagined. Once, I wrote that we could win and keep everything. But this time, I understand the cost. This time, the paladin cannot walk away from the fire. And neither can I.They say heroes always win. That the dawn always comes.But sometimes, night lingers.(And I wonder, if I had written it differently, would we have been saved?)Follows the events of the first two books. The only change-This is the ending I never meant to write.But it is the truest one I know.-M.W

summary:
When you become an adult, a lot of things change. You trade your previous set of priviliges and responsibilities for entirely new ones. And even before you turn eighteen, they share their experiences with you in hopes to teach you what to expect and prepare you for the harsh world ahead of you.But what do you do if your eighteenth birthday didn't go how you planned at all? In Phandalin, power does not belong to many. Only a handful of royal families rule within its walls, and among them stand the Shiventi. King Keier and Queen Evangeline have secured their lineage through their three sons and their youngest daughter, Lyra.
With her coming-of-age ceremony approaching, Lyra is expected to step into her role and prove herself worthy of the Shiventi name. But before she is given the chance, the foundation of her family begins to fracture.
Secrets surface. Tensions rise. And one by one, her brothers disappear, each chasing their own path, their own burdens, their own truths. Left behind in the wake of their absence, Lyra is forced to confront the weight of a name she isn’t sure she deserves.

If the Shiventi name is to survive, she cannot stand in their shadow any longer. She must find them. Before what once held them together is lost forever.

title: D&D Mechanics Redesign
author: Hailey Brightwater (HaileyBrightwater)
summary:
This is not a work of prose. Rather, this is a collection of posts modifying D&D classes and features in order to fit my narrative prose and stories. I see this collection as both an explanation and justification for what I write. Essentially, it's a tool to help me make sense of the classes I use in writing LitRPGs. Here you will find various "chapters" dedicated to either classes, spell lists, individual spells, or even an explanation or features that have been modified or replaced in order to better fit a story rather than a game.
The system I will be using is primarily D&D 5e as I find it the simplest to work with. However, I will be adding or modifying it with elements of D&D 3.5e and Pathfinder 1e which I like and find useful. It's definitely going to be out of balance from a player perspective; however, I think it will work much better in prose.
Everything is subject to change, including this summary; however, once I made a decision to include something in a written story in a particular way, I will try not to change it.

summary:
Thy mind is sunder’d, thy flesh is bound by oaths, and thy heart belongeth unto him who claimeth passion as his own.
He granteth thee promises of æternity, and each seemeth a solace—yet behind them lieth the price: thy freedom.
Thou seekest thyself, yet findest but new chains, e’ermore tightly entwining thee with him.
In a world of blood, of dominion, and of grey morality, no saviours dwell—only pain and obsession from which thine eyes may ne’er turn away.
And the voice of the Father whispereth in thy mind by night.This fic is conceived as a draft for a gothic novel that will later be rewritten into my own original setting and prepared for print.It’s inspired by the neo-gothic vibes of Lovecraft and Lukyanenko, and in terms of narration sometimes echoes Milton, Poe, Clark Ashton Smith, Anne Rice, and Clive Barker: pseudo-archaic language, body horror, psychological abuse, and religious motifs woven into a single story of dependence and cult.This is not the final version of the translation: I’m still polishing the style, rhythm, and wording, and I continue to revise even the chapters that are already published.

Mor smiled. “Hopefully my hands are still warm too. It’s why it took me longer to get your clothes.” She pressed her hands to his cheeks.

summary: Enver Gortash has always known exactly what Damien is. That's the problem.Set in the weeks before the Absolute's plans fracture into motion, the architecture of distance follows one night in which Damien , Bhaal's chosen, half-elf, a man who has built himself carefully and on his own terms, finds the walls he keeps between himself and Enver Gortash finally, irreparably compromised.Damien is five-foot-eight of scar tissue and controlled violence, black-eyed and sharp-faced, the kind of beautiful that looks like a warning. He was made from blood and bile, shaped by years of death into something that moves through the world like a predator, precise, watchful, difficult to surprise. He has fought for every inch of himself. He does not give ground easily.Gortash comes to deliver correspondence. He stays to take something apart. He does it quietly, the way he does everything, with patience and precision and the particular cruelty of a man who knows he's already won before the game begins. Damien knows he's being played. He has always known. It has never once been enough to stop it.The tension breaks. So does something else.

“I saw you on the ship, didn’t I?” the vampire asks, and Althea nods as much as she’s able, “Splendid. Now you’re going to tell me exactly what you and those tentacled freaks did to me.”
“I didn’t do anything, friend. They captured me just as they did you,” Althea responds evenly.

summary:
It's over. Astarion won. The hundredth year anniversary of his ascension was rapidly approaching and life had turned out better than Astarion could have ever dreamed of. A devoted wife, a beautiful son, and all the political power in Baldur's Gate he could hold in his sunkissed hands. Astarion was at peace after centuries of torment.
But in the shadow of the Vampire Ascendant lurked a figure from his past, the man who wore his face and shared his name. A shadow that could not bear the light and would forever pollute his mind. His peace was shattered by a mysterious letter, addressed to him by name.
To the Lord of the Crimson Palace, Astarion Ancunín,
Before you toss this letter into the bin or fireplace — I know where your brother is. If you don’t address this letter, I can assure you that you will never see him again.The forces hunting us are of a far greater magnitude than what is comprehensible to the physical mind. This entity will cut my family down and will not cease until yours is felled as well. It is near and the only solace we have is fleeing the coast — but it will find us. It will find you. We have one year.
Help us, Star.

title: Hold on to me, I'll hold on to you
author: Mushi_97
tags: 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) References
Inspired by Autumn a song by the strawbs
summary:
Halsin loves the way the earth does: patiently, indiscriminately, with roots that go deeper than anyone thinks to look. Astarion loves the way a man loves who was never taught it was safe to: silently, cautiously, with his armour on and his hands shaking underneath. And Gale loves the way a man loves who doesn't believe he deserves to: wholly, recklessly, giving every part of himself away and keeping nothing back, as though tenderness is something he must earn by spending it all on others first.
There is no word for what they are. Not lovers, not partners, not family, every word is too small. They are just the people who keep showing up. Who know every unglamorous corner of each other's souls and stay anyway. Just a cozy autumn sunday with hands in hair, lazy kisses that are nothing more than a kiss on a shapeless sofa, rain on old brick, and a song about seasons changing and holding each other through winter playing on a record so worn it's a miracle it still tracks.

summary:
After a night out with friends, Ada is ripped from her comfortable yet melancholy life in Frankfurt and wakes up on a mindflayer ship. She finds herself transformed into a Tiefling, and equipped with magical abilities she neither understands nor controls. Overwhelmed, confused and tadpoled, she teams up with other survivors to find a cure and, hopefully, make her way home.Ada finds that reluctant allies can, in fact, become friends over time, that she can learn to lean on them, and that there is more than one way to be strong.Then, there is this wizard with a mysterious condition who is eager to hear all her tales of this other world. As she starts to fall for Gale, Ada begins to confront the hurtful lies she has internalised about herself and finds a way to let herself be loved.
This is an isekai Galemance long-fic that covers one day of the journey in each chapter. For the most part, it follows the events of the game, with some changes made for either convenience or to heighten the yearning. This story covers themes such as religious trauma, fatphobia, queerphobia, bigotry and mental illness. There will be a somewhat happy ending, even if it is bittersweet. I currently publish about a chapter a month.

Isobel groaned when she disappeared out of view, presumably to do the fuselage or the tail, but soon enough she was back and gliding gracefully into her basket. summary:
“Ellia, it is a genuine pleasure.” He held his right hand out once more. She stared at the bandages, now slightly out of place by her pulling, and the slivers of exposed skin beneath: dark, purpling grey with a cracked-stone texture. Flashes of injuries and maladies skittered across her mind—nothing matched what she saw in him.
“I don’t want to hurt you,” she said with an indicating nod.
His smile turned wry. “Believe me, the damage there has already been done. But perhaps you’re right, and this will be better.” He swapped one hand for the other. A moment’s hesitation, then she accepted. His touch was warm. His skin more worn, more lived-in, than what she’d expected from a study-bound wizard. She wondered, dimly, what he felt in her hand. If the illusion would hold true under such direct connection, and what would happen if he realized who she truly was. But then his hand was gone and her wondering went with it. It didn’t matter. They wouldn’t be together long.
A novelization of BG3, reframed as a romance between Gale and a resistant Durge with alternating POVs. Elements of concept Gale. More Alfira. More Tara. More reactivity to Durge actions. Puns.

summary: What if the gods weren't done with the Dovahkiin once her adventures ended? When her missions were completed, and the dragons were soon to be conformed to learning the ways of the voice closely? When she was no longer needed within the realm of Tamriel? A place where the people she follows without question knew that here, she would learn something she had never learnt before, a lesson she would keep with her through the remaining eternity she will roam the world for. The lesson of love.---"Astarion, stop, you know we can't keep going like this" I said, lightly shoving the vampire away, not knowing truly whether I meant it or not. If you were to show Luciana her ability scores, she’d lament even more that she was raised in a community cut off from the Weave, because it’s painfully obvious that she should have been a wizard. She’d be insulted by the abysmal WIS score, think on it, and then begrudgingly agree. She’d laugh at the CHA score, assuming it must be a mistake. Because she has far too much stage fright for actual charisma.
Unfortunately for everyone including her, Luciana doesn’t know she’s in a game, and on the day she decides she should get one free murder as a treat, the realms seem to have conspired to land her on the biggest stage imaginable. She’d be mad, except her Patron did promise her all and everything and forever. She’s not sure she wants it anymore, because as it turns out, the world contains a lot more suffering than her sheltered upbringing prepared her for.

title: Intermission
author: PretzelCat
summary:
The tiefling set their rapier down on the stone beside them, placed the two large broken pieces of wood in front of them, and pulled out their instrument.
The singing of their strings finally pierced the heavy quiet of the air as their bow zipped up and down like lightning. Soon, the wires began to glow and let off hot, white sparks.
They’d always liked the tune that came with this spell. They wished it were longer, but when it was done, a small but brilliantly warm fire was dancing cheerfully in the middle of the boards, illuminating the small rectangular space in orange light.
They held their palms out towards it with a low sigh.
The scrapes on their forearms from being knocked to the ground didn’t seem bad, though it was almost impossible to tell how widely they stretched across the tiefling’s already-scarlet skin. Their toe no longer hurt where it had collided with the stone wall. At least they’d had the instinct, in their blind rage, to kick with the foot that actually had a brown leather boot to protect it.—

summary:
“You’re mine now, darling,” Astarion whispers against sensitive, flushed tanned flesh. “Just mine,” as teeth drag innocently against a vein, not biting, not piercing, but there, so, so, intoxicatingly there. Gale feels lightheaded.
“You owe her nothing, she has no hold over you, not anymore. No, that is for me, and me alone. I do so dread to share, you know,” He purrs, and Gale lets out a bated breath-turned-whimper when Astarion’s lips make their way up his jaw and to his ear, taking the flesh between sharp points and nipping.
One of the wizard’s hands comes to brace himself, right atop and over the vampire’s unbeating heart. His fingernails dig into the leather armor that covers Astarion’s pale skin longingly, bordering on desperate. Gale doesn’t know why, doesn’t know how, but near every part of his body that makes him him, every bone, every cell, every atom that builds his soul, is begging him to simply let the vampire take. For him to ravish, and bite, and suck, to take and take and take, until it’s inconceivable to him where Gale Dekarios ends, and Astarion Ancunín begins.
Oh, how he wants.
How he craves.

They didn't send a Bhaalist, Gortash realized, blankly. They sent a Bhaalspawn.
There had been rumors, of course; there were always rumors. None from anyone he'd consider remotely trustworthy, though, given that few could have knowingly laid eyes on one and survived to gossip.
What other explanation could there be? This thing, this beast devouring its prey mere feet away from him—there was no semblance of rational thought in the way its eyes burned in hunger and feral delight. Gortash gripped his small knife harder, and wished he'd brought something with a little more punch to it. He couldn't just stand here all night, however, plastered against the wall, hoping he'd somehow escape the creature's notice. Surely it was an optimistic sign that he still drew breath?

The pain and anger had leached from his face, leaving behind only the man, beautiful, vulnerable, solemn, hungry, and so, so tired. Have dinner with me.”An exploration of an older, selfish, and experienced Tav, defined by her quest for power and need for control—and Astarion, who might have bitten off more than he can chew. summary:
You cannot build a life together until you learn how to live your own.
In 1962, at a boarding school in Vermont, Astarion Ancunin meets the one person who makes life feel less like something to endure. Orphaned young and raised in Geneva by his exacting benefactor, Cazador Szarr, he grows up learning that stability is fragile and affection is conditional, shaping himself into someone controlled, private, and careful not to be left behind.
Rensaire Delaurin lives in the opposite direction—restless, musically brilliant, and always chasing the next stage, the next city, the next high. Over the next twenty-five years, their bond deepens and breaks as fame, distance, and old wounds pull them apart, forcing each of them to learn who they are on their own.
By 1987, Astarion has built a quiet life on the English coast—until a medical emergency brings Rensaire back to him, shaken, memory fractured, and very much alone. Given time and distance from the past, they are offered something they never had before: The chance to meet again as whole people—and to learn that sometimes, even after everything, it isn’t too late to begin again.

title: Bloodkiss
author: Bylmaresh
tags: Astarion is Bad at Feelings (Baldur's Gate)
Quest: The Pale Elf | Astarion's Companion Quest (Baldur's Gate)
Spoilers for Quest: The Pale Elf | Astarion's Companion Quest (Baldur's Gate)
summary:
So we lay there in the silent darkness on his bed. Our bodies entwined and as close to each other as possible. With every sip he took from me, the tension inside me grew, this bottomless longing for connection, for intimacy, and the shivering became stronger. Memories of our first night together after the celebration with the Tieflings whirled around in my head. The feel of his skin beneath my fingers, his hungry kisses. His indescribably talented hands. All the sweet words that went straight to my heart. Almost desperately, I ran my fingers through his hair, wanting only to feel him even closer to me -
Far too quickly, Astarion pulled away and looked down at me, breathing heavily. A small trickle of my blood ran down his chin. It was such a harsh contrast to his almost white skin that it seemed to glow even in the darkness. His gaze was grave, almost angry, which put a sharp damper on my desire. Had I done something wrong? When he stood up in one swift movement, I sat up too.
"Go."

summary:
A memoryless Dark Urge and a freshly unchained vampire spawn make an uneasy bargain: hunt, survive, and don’t let the world decide what they are. But old conditioning doesn’t die quietly—and neither does hunger.
 Author’s Note:Nex is a tiefling, but I have kept descriptors to a minimum to allow for reader immersion.
Thanks for reading. This story is a dive into the why beneath the masks: Dark Urge as a real hunger, Astarion as someone learning bodily autonomy in real time, and both of them unlearning old conditioning. Slow-burn, partnership to romance. Later chapters include explicit intimacy; consent is treated as non-negotiable (in-world, without modern phrasing). They are what destiny has left to the world, and they are what destiny wishes for the world.

title: Darling, Invite Me In
author: lolu
summary:
In the early days, when Astarion had first set out to seduce Tav in order to secure his loyalty, he’d thought the wizard was as easy to read as an open book. He wasn’t so sure anymore. As their bond deepened, instead of gaining clarity, Astarion found himself more and more often second-guessing what was going on inside Tav’s head. Too frequently, when Tav looked at him with those sharp, unreadable eyes, Astarion found himself at a loss for words.

  He was losing control over this - whatever this was.

  Astarion had perfected the art of seduction over nearly two centuries, but with Tav, he was entering uncharted territory.

  How did he even end up here?
#As their merry band of misfits arrives in the Lower City, Astarion feels the shadow of his former master looming larger than ever. Haunted by his past and the inevitability of facing Cazador again, he finds himself grappling with something entirely new: the uncertainty of being in a relationship. As he struggles to navigate these unfamiliar waters, he begins to realise he’s not the only one interested in Tav.

author: softbunnism
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
In the heart of Waterdeep, Gale Dekarios is a man of many titles: Archmage, Professor of Magical Theory, and former Chosen of Mystra. But to Tav, a teacher of the city's youngest and most rambunctious minds, he is simply the man who forgets his boots in the hallway and takes his tea with far too much honey.
While Gale spends his days lecturing on the complexities of the Weave, Tav spends hers navigating the chaos of the alphabet and crayon masterpieces. Their worlds are vastly different, yet they find a perfect, quiet harmony in their shard home - balancing ancient scrolls with lesson plans, and wine-soaked evenings with dreams of a future together. When the conversation shifts from magical theory to the possibility of their own legacy, Gale and Tav must prepare for their most daunting adventure yet: parenthood. From enchanting cradles to baby-proofing a wizard's toward, they discover that while magic can move mountains, it's the simple love between two people that can truly change the world.

title: Graceless
author: hollowharp

summary:
Gale Dekarios, chosen of Mystra, visits the Quiet Veil with one goal: find information on the Netherese artifact which will secure Mystra's favor. Eirael Frostflow clings to piety to overcome the frost—her blood curse—but will not forsake her vow of Day-Silence for anyone, chosen or not.
When they speak, it is under the shroud of night. The convent murmurs scandal.
***
Eirael captures his sleeve. Then the frost creeps up her neck and her eyes clamp shut. During the seconds she spends managing her breathing, Gale leans toward her. As if he has a right to indulge his impulse, closing the distance.
“Sister Eirael, you have my word, I will not let harm come to your books.” He tries his best reassuring smile when her eyes peek open. “I just need…”
His gaze drifts to the stained glass depiction of Mystra that backlights her.
“Peace,” he finishes, though that isn’t truly the word he means.
Her eyes are softer when his attention returns to her, and her grip on his sleeve relents with a cold caress of her palm against the fabric. It is wet.
“It’s only water,” he says. “It isn’t harmful.”
She nods once, sighs, and offers him a tight smile. Peace.

Izumi Midoriya's Quirk was nothing like her mother's, or the woman who'd carried her and dumped her on her mom when she was a baby.  It gave her nearly impenetrable chitin.  It gave her enhanced strength.  It gave her claws able to tear through steel.  It gave her blood stronger then any acid that she knew of.
And it made her a monster in the eyes of the world.  Almost everyone saw her as a villain in the making.  Almost everyone saw her as a soon-to-be killer.
But she didn't want that.  She wanted to be a Hero.  To be like All Might.  Even if her Quirk made her look like a monster.
And then her Quirk decided that merely looking like one wasn't enough, and started trying to coax her into mass slaughter through devouring and digesting, with the promise of EXP, levels, and so much more.
Katsumi would follow her no matter what.  The world would judge her harshly, no matter what.

summary:
After weeks in the wilderness, the group has finally reached an inn, with a fireplace, a bed, and solid walls - things that Astarion is determined to take full advantage of, now that he and Tav are more comfortable together. Astarion is thrilled that his plan is coming along so nicely - it means they can enjoy each others company, indulge in a footrub while they build up to the main event, maybe even find a way to make Tav more vocal in what she wants.
But their increased bond also means that Tav is getting braver.... and she's starting to ask questions he has no answer to.***“Here,” she breathed, lifting her chin to expose her throat. “I want.... want your fangs inside me.”
It was a ridiculous thing to say. He could tell from her face that she knew it as soon as the quiet words left her hesitant lips, and regretted it. If it was someone else, he'd have mocked them for it, raised his eyebrow and let a smug smile wash over his face. But she was trying, he thought fondly, and he knew it wasn't easy for her. So he pressed his lips against her neck, kissing as he worked his way to her ear.
“That's good,” he crooned, feeling her relax, ankles interlocking around his waist. “That's perfect, darling.”

He pledged to end all life and existence in his father's name! He, he—" He winds his hand through his hair, at a loss. "He was the mastermind behind the Absolute plot. Worked with Gortash and Ketheric Thorm. Helped Gortash use the Crown of Karsus on the elder brain to create a soulless army of mindflayers. He's the reason why I have a tadpole in my eye. Why we all do! He's the reason we're here, why we've been fighting and running all across Faerûn. I ... I had no doubts about supporting him before, when he was a Bhaalspawn fighting against his nature. I promised to protect him, to believe the best in him. But now? “He saw me, where Mystra didn’t.”
It’s late now. Astarion sits with Gale beneath the starless night and watches him polish his sword. A slip of the blade draws blood; unfazed, Gale brings his finger to his lips, and tastes it with naked rapture. In the waning moonlight, the rot is more obvious than ever before. Astarion hums softly. “Bhaal?”

A pause. Overhead, the wind is silent.

summary:
Strixhaven is home to the most wonderous of mages, the ones to seek out adventure and magic at the peril of death. These are the mages that know magic is a spectrum and how easy it is to be drawn in by the darkness. And yet there are still others who seek to be swallowed by the darkness. Dendra joined Strixhaven after being disinherited from her father's company, Phantomedia. With no resources and a dwindling reputation, she elects to disenfranchise herself altogether, traveling to her father's alma mater. There she finds company with a past like her own, goals and dreams she can't even imagine, and a greater purpose than the one she was robbed of.
NOTE: all characters (except Dendra) are original characters that belong to other creators. This work is largely a peak into the world of Strixhaven (modified by our lovely DM) through Dendra's eyes and may result in inaccurate portrayals of such characters. Jins leans even closer to watch, one hand braced on the glass while the other still rests protectively over their stomach. Ubiquity tries very hard not to think about how natural it feels to stand this close to them, or how instinctively he shifts so their shoulders touch.“So,” Jin says casually, eyes on the moving claw. “You’ve been weird today.”Ubiquity’s hand nearly slides clean off the joystick. “Wha–? Weird?”“Mm.” Jin hums. “Fidgety too. What’s going on?”The claw descends too early and grabs nothing but air. It rises again, empty, and Ubiquity exhales through his nose.“Maybe…I just wanted to hang out.”Jin gives him a look that says they know him far too well for that answer to hold. It’s not pushy, though, just…patient. Soft. Waiting with their eyes glued to Ubiquity’s hand as he urges the claw onwards again.

summary: “Mystra-ryl! My car!” Gale shouted, walking around to see someone with large sunglasses looking down at them from the height of their ridiculously tall vehicle. The tint of the windshield made it difficult to see them, Gale could make out short, curled hair and a pale complexion as he began to step closer. ”Hullo? summary:
It has been several days now since my escape from the Mind Flayers, and I feel no closer to finding a cure for the parasite they buried in my skull. What's more, I still can't seem to recall anything of my life before the crash. I'm not sure whether my amnesia is the result of my mind being slowly consumed by my unwanted passenger, or the symptom of some, even darker affliction.
Still, my newfound companions seem capable, and are all eager to discover a way to rid ourselves of our parasites. Hopefully, if we work together, we will be able to find a cure before we lose ourselves to the plot of whatever it is that has infected us. At least this will make for an incredible story should we live long enough to see it through.--
Journal entries of a Half Drow Bard who has found themselves suffering amnesia after falling from a Mind Flayer ship. This is a series I am writing to go along with my first time Durge play-through of the game. It follows my original Durge, Loric, as he explores the land and tries to discover who he was before the parasite, and meets the cast of Baulder's Gate 3.

summary:
Nemesis does not remember the man who calls himself her ally. She remembers blood, steel and fragments of a past carved out of her skull.
She remembers the Urge.
The story begins the eve of Enver Gortash’s coronation. Baldur’s Gate celebrates its new Archduke while Nemesis and her companions are honored guests through their newfound alliance forged in strategy rather than trust.
But Gortash remembers more than she does. And throughout the festivities, beneath chandeliers and polite applause, behind carefully measured smiles, he begins to press at the cracks in her missing memories. With charm, with insinuation and with the quiet certainty of someone who knows she once belonged at his side.
Nemesis does not know whether she wants to kill or remember him. And in Baldur’s Gate, both may lead to the same ending.

title: The Last Will and Testament of Cazador Szarr
author: AbigailMoment
tags: Trying To Be A Good Person In A Terrible Situation
But Has Trouble Appreciating Them Because Trauma
A Curiously Large Amount of Fluff
summary:
"First," said Gale. "Do not kill any thinking creatures in Waterdeep unless you must to protect yourself or you have my express permission."
As Gale spoke, he could feel the weight of his words sinking into the person sitting across from him. It was like casting a spell, but took no effort. Astarion had been staring hollowly into his goblet of blood, but at this he made a faintly interested noise. As if the rule were novel and he was considering the shape of it.
"Second, you will obey me in all things," said Gale. There didn't feel like there was any honest way of softening that. Astarion didn't make any sound at all.
"Third, do not leave the tower without permission." Astarion made another speculative noise, considering this one too. But then his shoulders hunched and his eyes skittered down, as if he didn't want to look at what was about to happen.
"Fourth," Gale said, and paused. He started with some context: "There is a tressym upstairs."
Astarion's head twitched. He looked up at Gale, blinking, startled. He had the air of someone who had been bracing for a blow and instead had just been handed a balloon animal.
"A what?" he asked.

Astarion's back is to Gale, but Gale knows his tells. He can see the vampire is fidgeting with his hands, looking down at them. His shoulders are tense and hunched.
Gale takes a step closer and Astarion's head snaps up, nose in the air proudly. "Gale, it's not my fault so many renters hate vampires. Or perhaps they just hate bloodstains. And I am a dreadfully messy eater."
Gale crosses his arms over his chest. "And what about the place we looked at a few days ago? The one with the green cabinets and the patio. The renter is a vampire! It would be perfect for you!"
"You mean the place with the crown moldings? Can you see me dusting crown moldings?" He holds an offended hand to his chest.
Gale huffs a breath through his nose which Astarion thinks sounds quite like a scoff. "I can't see you dusting anything, Astarion. But you've got to find a place eventually. Your case is being shown to board members. You can't stay forever."
 
Astarion is living at a halfway house for crime victims. Gale, his counselor and advocate, has been pushing him to move on for a whole year.
I wonder why he doesn't want to leave...

summary:
“There are angels just like you,” he spoke, and fire
Twined through my mind, a chain I could not break.
“They linger high, yet Heaven’s winged desire
Covets what we share, the world to shake.
No one will match your beauty, and none like me,
And should you seek, it only drives the ache.
Each whisper of my name will pull, you see,
And leave your soul to tremble, wide awake.”
 
Six years have passed since they were torn apart.
Every time Cazador reminds him of his 133-year “mistake,” the shame presses firmer into his ribs, a constant reminder of what was lost. What he'd had.
Astarion wonders what it was all for—every stolen moment together, every cruel lesson in return, and the ever-increasing shadowed years building.
And finally, he decides: If he cannot reach the sun, nor bask in its light… then he will simply leap toward it.

Dear Readers,
I, Abbi, always believed alien abduction was plausibly real, but it was for other people. Maybe, aliens like abducting people who are mentally ill so it seemed like they are lying. Maybe, that's why I ended up on the nautiloid. Or maybe, I wasn't supposed to.
Either way, whether by design or by accident, I got to see a world saved. Even if it was technically just a tiny corner of it and not even my own.
Sometimes, it takes just a random group of people motivated to solve the same problem to make a difference, one step at a time. At the behest of my companions, I’m getting my adventure on paper. Sometimes the gods really are listening. And sometimes they're just cunts.
Cheers to the Heroes of Baldur's Gate and, hopefully, we can get a more accurate retelling down since Volo's was — please, don't read it. We didn't have a dragon with us, just a dragonborn.

title: Baby, It's Cold Outside
author: HamartiaGrander
tags: no beta we die like Mizora. yay!
summary:
Wyll had never been good at wanting things. It always came with a tremendous amount of guilt that almost made the things he wanted no longer worth it. But even with the guilt, his heart had never ceased its dreadful longing, and that had only grown the longer Wyll spent away from Astarion. Now that he was here, sitting in front of Wyll and smiling as though no time had passed at all, Wyll’s heart wanted nothing more than to rip itself from his chest and take permanent residence in Astarion’s hands.
Instead, Wyll hid the nervous clearing of his throat behind the sound of the tap water, and hung the rag over the side of the basin to dry. He turned back to Astarion, resuming his professionalism.
"What can I get you, my friend?” he asked.
~
It's been a year since they defeated the Netherbrain, and Wyll has made a life for himself out in the wilds of the Sword Coast. When Winter comes, and Wyll sequesters within a tavern inn, he's joined by an old friend who hasn't left his mind - or his heart - even after all this time.

summary:
This is just an idea I had and wanted to get off my mind because I need sleep and I don't have the energy to write a full-fledged story. People can use this prompt/idea for their own fanfics if they'd like:
Centuries ago, the Earth's population discovered soul marks. It was what was said to bring the end of wars, and propelled human into furthering technology and aiming for a more peaceful future.
It was working, until a bunch of spaceships appeared and kidnapped a number of the humans.
Placed into stasis, possibly for centuries, the survivors wake up after a crash landing in a completely different world that appears to closer to a medieval era than the futuristic one that they know. So, they decided to sort themselves out in a place far away from the main populace, so as not to repeat the history of their more 'barbaric' ancestors.
Of course, that's when our favorite, chaotic group decides to investigate.

warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
tags: Novelization trying to stay as canon as possible
Other Additional Tags to Be Added
I don't skip to the sex we take the scenic route

summary:
As a group of reluctant allies fight to stop the encroachment of the Absolutist cult, they cling to each other for support as they fight their personal battles as well. And through vulnerability and kindness, they all begin to heal.
A love letter to Baldur's Gate 3, the game that lives in my brain and stole my heart. Features three original characters based on ones I created in the game: Faen, pronounced "Fain" (F), Tav (M) and Amaranda (F). It starts off pretty dark, gets worse before it gets better, but everyone in the party pairs up, good defeats evil and love, kindness and friendship conquer all.
This is a novelization adaptation of sorts, written for old fans, new fans, and the curious. The idea is that anyone can just start reading, even if they know nothing about the game. My eventual goal is to convey all the drama, humor, redemption, and express why I love these characters and their journey, to everyone, especially people who can't get into playing the game for whatever reason.
Any explicit scenes (or parts of scenes) are flagged at the beginning of the chapter notes, with specific warning tags listed. They're written so you won't miss any story beats if you choose to skip them.

Generations of interbreeding and intermixing make the idea of a standard Fantasy Race a legendary myth. Mortals have moved past their ethnic differences of the past and instead move towards the conflicts of politics and nations.
Xharline de Ouissaint seeks an apprenticeship with the oldest and most powerful living mage to escape a betrothal she does not wish.
Tyromir Schwanloch wishes to be a simple agent of the crown, and not be responsible for the lives of his new soldiers.
Vaelin Talgia Saarun-Dharn is a young person looking for a future - they find it aboard an airship piloted by a legendary adventurer as dangerous as she is charming
And above it all, the Skull Lord is locked in a chess match for the fate of Reality against a foe he cannot find, and Science and Magic meld to create things undreamed by Gods or Mortals. It is an era of change in the Profane Era, and no one knows what will happen next.

summary:
Lightning crawls across his claws when he wakes.
Not to the crash of battle. Not to the screams of cultists or the whisper of a god in his skull.But to rot. Filth. An unfamiliar sky framed by the walls of a narrow alley.
He remembers victory. The fall of the Netherbrain. His companions alive. The world saved.
He remembers dying.
Bhaal’s gift still coils in his veins. The storm still answers his call.
But his name is gone.
Strangers stare at his scales and call him a freak. They speak of “heroes” and “quirks,” of powers born not from the Weave but from blood and chance. This world has no gods he knows. No devils he’s bargained with. No one who understands what he is.
And when threatened, when cornered, when action is needed-The Urge answers.Teeth. Claw. Lightning.
In a society built on heroes and villains, what place is there for something that is neither?
The Dark Urge has fallen into a new world.And it may soon learn to fear him.

It was about a year after the defeat of the Absolute and Seraphina an aasimar, a descendant of Lathander, had failed in her mission. She had fallen in combat against the vampire ascendant, but before her soul could be collected by her beloved Morning lord, suddenly she was thrown back into a dark empty cold place.
She was in a cold tight box with an ache in her stomach, she punched through the wood easily and dug her way out of the dirt, had someone buried her while she was still alive? But that didn't make sense, she felt empty, cold on the inside, like most of her divine light had abandoned her.

summary:
I never imagined I'd survive the tadpole. That mind flayer attempted to transform me into one of its own, taking away my will. Back then, I wasn't alone; I had Enfer, Astarion, Karlach, Wyll, Gale, Shadowheart, Lae'zel, and Halsin. We made it through the terror together, but I should have listened to Astarion and Shadowheart about that 2 a.m. walk. That night, I was kidnapped. Ten years later, I'm stuck inside a pod aboard a Drow ship in the skies. This fate is shared by four strangers: Adelaide, Nabrim, Daniel, and Sapphire. They don't know me, but I'm going to need them. My palm throbs with a purple mark, pulsating with a terrible need, a reminder of the control that still exists. The ship pitches, the storm yells, and I know the fight hasn't ended. My blood demands what it needs, but I've been through worse. I'm also capable of surviving this. Every second counts, every decision could mean the difference between life and death, and these strangers may be the only thing keeping me connected to what remains of me.

summary:
"I know Mielikki is with me because I sense her. I feel her touch as the wind. I hear her voice in the whisper of leaves. I see her beauty in the scene around us. Her presence is as real as yours. She embraces us with every reverent step we take in the wilderness."-The words of a favored of Mielikki
The main story revolves around Astarion’s relationship with Tavennia, a kind-hearted Cleric of Mielikki. Tav is on the run from an abusive marriage and quickly learns that she and Astarion have far more in common than she would ever have imagined.
This work is canon adjacent and includes some canon dialogue and spoilers, but it is not always fully canon compliant. It it intended to be a "what if". Not something that did happen, but something that could have happened in between the lines. In canon, Astarion prayed to the gods for help and was never answered. But what if one goddess heard him and it just took him a while to figure that out?
This is a story about love’s ability to mend even the most tortured of hearts.
I hope you enjoy it.

title: Naughty by December
author: anarchy_amaryllis
summary:
In this modern AU story, Leto embarks on an unexpected journey of intimacy and self-discovery after receiving a spicy advent calendar meant to be playful, indulgent, and a little daring. Each chapter follows a new day, and a new door, revealing an item, sensation, or idea that challenges her expectations. What begins as mild curiosity quickly turns into moments of embarrassment, frustration, laughter, and growing intrigue.
Through each experience, Leto navigates her own boundaries, insecurities, and desires, supported by Halsin’s steady, attentive presence. Rather than focusing solely on the items themselves, the story centers on communication, trust, and emotional safety, showing how intimacy can be built slowly through reassurance, patience, and mutual respect. Some days spark excitement, others hesitation, but every chapter becomes a step toward deeper understanding, of herself and of their relationship.
As the calendar unfolds, the tone balances warmth, humor, and sensuality, transforming small surprises into meaningful shared moments. By the final chapters, the calendar is no longer just about spice or novelty, but about connection, comfort, and choosing to explore together.

summary:
A quiet retreat in the Pacific Northwest becomes the birthplace of Velvet Ember’s second album — and something more difficult to name. As music, fiction, and lived emotion begin to blur, Gail Dekarios and Astarion find themselves circling a truth they aren’t ready to announce, only to recognize.

title: BALDUR’S WALL: Behind the Wall - A Mockumentary
author: Vestagirl
summary:
Baldur’s Wall: Behind the Wall is a mockumentary-style collection of transcripts, interviews, rehearsal footage, and recovered production notes from a rock opera that absolutely should not have existed—and yet somehow did.
Years after the original Baldur’s Wall rock opera was written, a chaotic ensemble of heroes, villains, scholars, and self-appointed directors attempt to document how it all came together. What begins as a behind-the-scenes retrospective quickly unravels into conflicting memories, theatrical egos, inexplicable casting decisions, and the growing realization that the Wall itself may have been more than metaphor.
Told through unreliable narrators, fragmented footage, and increasingly questionable production choices, Behind the Wall explores what happens when myth becomes performance, performance becomes truth, and no one is entirely sure who was supposed to be in charge.
This is not the story of the show.
This is the story of everything that went wrong—and somehow still mattered.

title: Losing My Religion
author: a_non_y_mit_y
summary:
A pair of shoes entered Shadowheart’s line of vision as she reeled from the release of the pod. She slowly looked up to see who they belonged to, who her savior was. She was taken aback just looking at the woman towering over her. Her skin was a perfect mix of blue and purple, a deep indigo blushing across her cheeks and the tips of her pointed ears. There was a gap in her front teeth as she smiled down at Shadowheart, her lips the same shade as color on her cheeks. Her eyes were deep purple, almost as dark as her pupils. White curtain bangs framed her face, the rest of her hair pulled back in a low ponytail. White eyebrows and eyelashes framed her eyes.
The next thing Shadowheart noticed was the Selûnite symbol dangling from her earrings. She didn’t say anything, even though she wanted to. Even though she normally would. Perhaps this woman could ruin Shadowheart. Perhaps she already had.

summary:
Over half a century has passed since the fall of the elder brain in Baldur’s Gate and the disappearance of Edmé d’Aurianne-Soares (Tav) into the Shadowfell. In that time, Astarion Ancunín has been able to find himself. Instead of stabbing enemies, he stabs sewing needles into pincushions as a tailor in Waterdeep. Instead of getting out of trouble with charm, he uses his wit to find loopholes in contracts as a lawyer.
But many of his friends and partners have grown old or passed away, and, as nice and busy as Waterdeep can be, Astarion finds himself wanting to see more of the world like he always imagined he would with his freedom. 
A couple months ago, Astarion received a letter about two of Cazador Szarr’s other spawn who wanted to reunite. He took that opportunity with a simple trip in mind, only to embark on another journey into the Shadowfell because of suspicious blood trade rumors. There, he finds that old ends weren’t as tied up as he thought. Edmé re-enters his existence unaged, the two of them a lot more similar than they once were.

“And you,” he says, voice low and dangerous now, every word sharpened to a point, “you talked me out of it.”
The accusation lands hard.
“You stood there,” he continues, stepping closer, eyes blazing, “looking at me like I was about to commit some terrible mistake - as if I hadn’t already lived through centuries of them.” His laugh is bitter, broken. “As if you hadn’t already decided you knew better.”
His hands shake as they curl into fists. “You told me I didn’t need it. That I didn’t need power. That I didn’t need to become something more.”
He closes the distance between them almost entirely. He's near enough now to lunge for her neck.After Cazador’s death, Astarion is left with the weight of a choice he didn’t take.
Angry, raw, and convinced he threw away his only chance at being whole, he turns that fury on Tav - the one who stood beside him when it mattered most.

Aeterna Amantes, lovers forever… or so they thought. Two hundred years after the Battle for the Gate, two hundred years after Lyra joined Astarion in eternity as his Dark Consort, the couple finds themselves living separate lives. title: Silk and Teeth (Astarion x Cazador)
author: AstarionsRat
summary:
“Stand at the foot of the bed. Back to me. Remove your shirt.”
Silk whispered away; cool air traced the lattice of scars Cazador had carved decades ago. Astarion squared his shoulders, braced for the whip, the crack, the inevitable command: Scream prettily for me, boy.
Silence stretched. No leather uncoiled. No manacles clinked. Only that gaze, boring into his neck—patient, deliberate, worse than any lash.
Then movement. A slow, deliberate press of a taller body behind him, brocade brushing bare skin, hardness grinding slow. A hitch tore from Astarion’s throat.
This wasn’t the script.
“Master…?” The word cracked, small.
Lips brushed his throat, not biting—not yet. “Hush, boy. I did not ask you to speak.”
Astarion’s mind reeled. He’d waited for this touch once, lifetimes ago—before the crypt, before the chains. But not like this. Not from him. His body betrayed him anyway: hips twitched back, chasing the thick ridge even as instinct screamed to flee.
Cazador chuckled, dark and pleased. “Good boy,” he whispered, grinding slow and filthy. “Now... let’s see how prettily you can moan.”

Compilation of all Night Sly stories occurring in Act One!
Failed priestess and chronic womanizer Neffeyla Qil'oussiryn never thought she'd amount to much without Lolth's guidance. So, she turned to the surface instead... until a certain kidnapping and crashed Nautiloid completely threw off her plans. But while the surface is a grim place, a certain dark and mysterious priestess has caught her eye, practically begging to get caught up in her web. And if the tadpole is going to kill them all, why not have some fun on the way out?
Shadowheart is nothing if not loyal to her goddess, Shar, which has often set her outside "good and decent" society. It's never something that bothered her... she thinks. It's hard to know for sure when you don't have any memories. It's also hard to understand what she feels when her mission fails and she's swept into an uneasy alliance with an unfamiliar drow, whose flirtatious intentions seem suspicious at best, and threatening at worst. Lufian - Signifying deep affection for someone or something.
How true it was. That he was willing to do anything for his Goddess.
How undeniable it is, that he is nothing without her. Without the Weave.
And now? Well, Gale was bestowed a way in which he could be forgiven.
It was a bittersweet notion, that stole breath from already emaciated lungs. To no longer be under her scrutinising disappointment. title: Eye to Eye
author: herringbone (thewovenwheel)
summary:
Eli finds Shadowheart tucked away in the shade beneath those squat, crumbling rock faces, bushes crawling from cracks in the cliffs, shielded by the shrubbery from the campsite proper. Here, the talking in the clearing blends into an indiscernible slurry of sound, easy enough to pack away; Shadowheart is silent, on her knees with her feet tucked under her skirt, hands clasped into a palmless amalgamation of pale knuckles. (She has always had interesting hands; narrow-fingered, with careful-placed calluses, and a ragged little sore like a needle-nick or a cigar burn dug out of the place where the basilic vein splits into branches. They’re not like Eli’s hands, long and double-jointed and satin-soft. Eli likes them.) Her fringe is a sharp black line against her forehead. Her head is bowed. What little sun creeps over the steep rock slope catches on the delicate chains woven around her hair, and they shine so starkly it stings Eli’s eyes.
Eli sets herself down in the grass, cross-legged and dew-brushed, and, picking at the tough fabric of her trousers, she settles in to wait.

Lord Smallpiece of Ashwood has a problem.  His Great-Uncle Algy has gone missing... and so has his coffin.  Algy is the only known non-evil vampire in the D&D universe, and he had been doing a great job as the mansion's night guard.
So Lord Smallpiece decides to hire Glodric Innkeepersson, a high-level wizard, to get him back; and Glodric can't do the job on his own, so he ropes in three friends - Kerian Pitchpipe, the most famous bard in the world; Master Reinart the Artificer, a sorcerer with a very nice line in constructs; and Lindith Nimblehands, non-affiliated cleric and inveterate multi-crafter. title: 生命本身 (Life Itself)
author: JZar
relationships: The Dark Urge/Orin the Red (Baldur's Gate)
summary:
“这篇记录用深色墨水写在一沓信纸上，属于一位不久前逝去的深水城著名法师及教授的遗物。手稿详细记载了一位巴尔后裔的生平，活跃于夺心魔威胁下的 ‘大恐慌‘ 年代。文中提及了击败敌人主脑的英雄小队成员，其中的队长正是文章的讲述者乔安娜——博德之门的拯救者竟拥有如此平凡的名字。文中的许多角色经过证实确认为存在过的人物，假使这些文字是真实的，其主人公也无法再被找寻，所有能追踪到她的痕迹早已蒸发在人世间，仅有这篇记录证明了她的存在。如今巴尔教团在费伦大陆也销声匿迹，有关巴尔之子的报告也不再更新。诚然，许多事实显示巴尔后裔生性残忍嗜血，缺乏人性，但记录的作者坚称即使是如此的生物也拥有自我控制，以及更为重要的，悔改的能力。文中还包括了对于死亡之境，古代神明和禁忌科技的描述，同样，我们也无从证明这些事物的真实性。尽管如此，此篇手稿经整理后被批准作为相关研究的辅助读物，为旧日时光的真容提供了亮丽的一瞥。”

Clytestra simply nods, her hair, as white as the snow that used to cover his fathers home during the winter, falls over her horns. Distantly, he feels bitter. She managed to make those so beautiful. A foolish thought, she had been born with them, they weren't a punishment from a contract broken, they were allowed to be beautiful.
 
It's only when Clytestra begins ruffling through her pack that Wyll realises he hasn't responded, just stared at her horns like some creep. He moves to apologies, but he's momentarily shocked out of it by the sight of her holding out a pillow towards him-Of all things! It's thinner than the usual ones he's seen before, but almost as thick as the ones in his old room when he was still welcome, made with some fabric he does not recognise.
 
Most likely, seeing the confusion, Clytestra shuffles forward a little awkwardly, "It's for your horns." She stops grimacing, "I know you're not used to them, so this should help."
----------

summary:
As the Goddess of Fate weaves her great tapestry of all the stories of the living and dead, she notices a few strands which hang loosely from the rest of the pattern. They might have once been a part of the grand storyline, however they no longer could be spun into the yarn; this one here was too tangled to be of use, this one here was of the wrong color, this one here was causing the tapestry to unravel... She mourns for a moment the many stories she had once planned, the fallen threads she must discard, but she smiles, for The Fates had given her a new muse, a new pattern to weave, divine inspiration greater than what she had originally designed. The Tapestry is much more vibrant, elegant, and the stitching is strong and immaculate through their guiding hands.
She pulls out a pair of golden shears, and severs the fallen threads.

summary:
He doesn't know what love is. All he knows is hunger.
He'd learned to live with it. The hunger had been his most faithful companion over the years, and he had long since given up the ghost of self-denial. He knew what he was. At least, he'd known before he'd woken up on that ravaged beach, blinking in the too-bright sun and you'd come stumbling down the dirt-worn path, covered in blood of questionable origin.
You play the part of the amnesiac hero with charm. None of your other companions seemed to detect there was something deeply, deeply monstrous within you. But he smells the blood your short fingernails draw from digging into your palms when you choke out pleasantries and diplomacy. He recognizes the glint of bloodlust in your eyes.
He watches you and he can just tell.
You know hunger, too.

summary: The world, Kraal, ‘ended’ a year and a half ago. Undead monsters of every kind seemed to pour in from every corner of land imaginable. The living of the world fled to safety, most survivors found themselves isolated and hard pressed for resources. The world environment consists of mostly desert and dry mountain regions. There are occasional forests and very limited plains, and only one single rainforest on the continent of Avvalone. This rainforest is rumored to be the very last safe space on the planet, the undead roaming the world seem to avoid the Ardan Rainforest, for reasons unknown. There are whispers of a rumor among the survivors of an entity with power capable of dispelling the accursed beings from the world that dwells deep in the rainforest, but no certain proof exists. The lands are littered with battle torn once great kingdoms, undead ravaged survivor camps, and small settlements of the still living.

title: A Kingdom of Khoravar
author: Mikael_Soterys
summary:
In the kingdom of Galifar, the Wynarn dynasty boasted of being a house of ancient lineage, having arrived in Khorvaire millennia ago—the oldest of all human families! However, this doesn't mean they are monolithic. Things change, love finds a way, and occasionally, a pair of pointed ears peeks out from among the leaves of the family tree. One half-elven king, Laeran, had such a tragic end (betrayed by his brother, no less!) that no one like him ever ascended the throne of the nation again, but why did this happen? There were others like him, and perhaps they can help us understand…
In this research work, the scribe Mikael Soterys delves into the history of the royal Khoravar and the misfortune behind their short reigns.

While attempting to enter the Sacred city of Myrnia; an unlucky Air Genasi stumbles into a series of very unfortunate situations that land him in quite the awkward position.
~~~
“Man, what… is wrong with you?” The question came in that rumbling voice, but it sounded different than those that had come before. Confused and almost concerned.
“You’re on fire, do you have a fever?” A cool hand touched Atropho’s forehead and his shaking stopped. Torn between desires; his brain urged him to flinch back and push into the touch at the same time.
So divided, he found himself unable to do either. Frozen like a stag that’d heard a twig snap. About to flee, about to fight… painfully unable to do either.
Atropho felt delirious, “whats wrong with me?? Fuck dude, whats wrong with You?” He fought for control, and casually as he could, lolled his head to the side. And did his best to ignore the jolt as he broke contact.

summary:
Many times in your life you’d been cautioned about rooting through any old chest. Many times you’d elected to entirely ignore that sage wisdom in favour of chance, the potential that you might find something of value that others had left behind. Didn’t those same wise people preach waste not, want not anyway? Besides, a refugee from Elturel like yourself with barely any possessions should be entitled to at least something to begin your life anew.
And even though far more recently you had been cautioned by a passing wizard that even books might be dangerous, it hadn’t stopped you from picking up the leatherbound tome that rested on your lap.
Your fingers traced over the cover, embossed with delicate gold, swirling patterns matching the ornate scripting that gave the author’s name – Volothamp Geddarm.What secrets does Volo's book hold? And why does the very thought of reading on make your heart flutter in your chest?...

summary:
Gale Dekarios does not come to Greyvale Manor looking for ghosts. He comes to outrun one. Recently widowed after his wife, Mystra, died in a devastating fire, he buries himself in science to explain grief, memory, and everything the mind refuses to release. When the mysterious owner of Greyvale invites him to investigate claims of paranormal activity, Gale accepts, hoping to rebuild his career and escape the shadow that still follows him.
He is not the only one summoned. Other researchers, sceptics, and professionals arrive, each carrying secrets and fears of their own. Among them is Sameera, a reluctant medium who has spent her life seeing what others refuse to face. From the moment she enters, she knows what the others do not.
Greyvale is not simply haunted. It is aware. It listens. It remembers.
Inside a house haunted not only by death but by everything the living bring with them, each of them must confront something far more terrifying than spirits:
The parts of themselves the manor refuses to let them escape.

summary:
Since the very near end of the world, and his subsequent planting of roots in Reithwin, Halsin has grown accustomed to waking alone.
It’s been strange, and lonely. He would never begrudge his partners for following their own paths, but it’s harder without them than he imagined it would be.
With morning comes the chirping of birds, the rhythmic hammering as Reithwin rises from its own ruins, the peals of children’s laughter. But it also brings a too-large bed, cold to the touch, and a house that doesn’t quite feel like a home.
It’s Halsin’s reality, ideal or not, which is why the difference is so stark when he wakes to the sensation of another’s body heat, warm in a way that the rising sun through the window can never compare to.

Until her mentor mysteriously disappears, her reality slips and falls, knocking its head against a firm corner, but instead of bleeding out - she recognizes things that previously seemed to be right in front of her the whole time, hidden in plain sight. Barry had promised to protect him, that nothing would happen to him while they were around—and against every instinct he’d built up throughout his enslavement, he’d believed them.
Barry turned to face him, tears now streaming down its face. Astarion’s carefully composed facade shattered at the sight, a mixture of concern and guilt flitting across his features.
“No, wait—I didn’t mean…” he said quickly, stumbling over his words.

summary: In the forgotten realms, east of the sword coast and south of the spine of the world, there is a city-state called Cathania. It is a new city, attempting to assert itself as a neutral state, founded on principles of tolerance, acceptance, and free trade. It's acceptance of everyone has made it a cultural mixing pot, and a target of other cities in the realm who abide by traditional notions of good and evil. Cathania is also a divine "dead-zone", effectively neutralizing the interference of the gods via magic. Clerics and Paladins cannot pray to the gods here for strength. This has created a mercenary haven, a market for items that can store and release power, and a reputation of Cathania as a "wretched hive of scum and villainy". Cathania is host to a variety of characters, namely Mordos Dread, a Warlock Tiefling who seeks peace after a life of violence and trauma, though it seems to always elude him. He is friends with Elrohius Rekvezant, a drow thief and rogue, Avaria Hawthorne the "Gold Monger" (the only paladin in cathania who has power), Fizzik Kant the drow assassin, and Prozar the infinite (human wizard who can't die until he fulfills a prophecy).They seek not to be heroes, but power, glory, and riches.

summary:
The recent, violent happenings taught the city caution: people chose their routine more carefully now, and many avoided being out after dark altogether. It did little good. The murders continued, and if anything, they had grown more frequent. The blades of Bhaal were proving more capable than Enver had first been inclined to give them credit for.
He was to meet their leader that very night. Securing the meeting had been no easy feat: the Bhaalist had proven elusive, and plainly uninterested in making his acquaintance. That is, until Enver found the right leverage, as he invariably did. He had learned early in his life that everyone had a price. If not in coin, then in power. If not in power, then in fear. One way or the other, there was always something that could be offered, threatened, or taken, something that made even the most resolute bend to his will.
In this case, information was the currency.
─────
How Gortash tracked down the Bhaalist behind the city’s bloodshed, and the meeting that would set the stage for everything to come.

When the world begins to fall out of harmony, the first to hear it is a bard.
Dina, a traveling musician trained in ancient traditions where stories shape reality, follows unsettling rumors from the frontier town of Briarholt into the lawless Unbound Marches. Villages have gone silent, magic misfires, and something old is stirring beneath the land’s broken rhythms.
As empires lie in ruin and the gods grow distant, Dina discovers that her songs can steady what should not be steady—and that every note she plays draws attention. Ancient forces listen for discord, feeding on imbalance and fear.

The first chord has been struck.

…boring… So I thought exchanging letters would make it suck less…eaten today yet? I hope you’re not lettin… half the food from your plate again. Don’t dragonborn need to eat a lot, especially when you’re growing? I’ve been… could be worse, I guess… You would’ve kicked all their asses, I bet…
Only the inconsequential needling and quibbling of a pathetic, needy child. Astarion crumples up the note and tosses in his unlit fireplace.

tags: Location: The Last Light Inn (Baldur's Gate)
summary: JAHEIRA'S FIELD REPORT: Documents the operational and personal transformation of two key party members under sustained pressure in the Shadow Cursed Lands. Gale enters under Mystra's death directive, tactically unreliable. Teague enters carrying an active infernal contract and unresolved self-concealment. Over the course of operations at Last Light Inn, both are stripped of their defensive architectures. Teague identifies a contractual loophole linking Gale's protection to her infernal obligations. Her backstory disclosure reveals sorcerous origin through childhood violence and self-taught bardic casting via the Song of Creation. Gale's response — protective fury modulated by intellectual fascination — establishes the dynamic governing their partnership. The arc's pivot is Gale's Weave-bonding proposal. Teague warns that spiritual merging with her bloodline carries hereditary consequences. He accepts. The bonding fundamentally alters his trajectory: he enters Act 2 resigned to self-sacrifice and exits committed to survival, crediting Teague's influence. Assessment: two operatives who entered this theater expecting to die have independently given each other reasons not to.

title: Experimental Theorems of Desire
author: Aerin67
summary:
Trapped in a ruined monastery and cut off from their companions, Gale and Tav are helpless when his arcane hunger strikes - and they have no magical items left to appease the orb. As detonation looms ever closer, Tav seizes on a desperate, dangerous idea that might just save them both.
---
Tav drew in a careful breath. The Weave that always hummed at the edge of her senses felt restless that day, churning inside her like a storm waiting for release. She was aware of it in every inch of her skin, in the slow roll of power at the base of her spine, in the tingling tips of her fingers.
“What about me?” she asked. “I’m magic.”
Gale stared at her, and for the first time since this started, looked genuinely thrown. “Tav, that is not how this works.”
“Are you sure?” Her voice was steady, but her heart had picked up, beating in time with that strange second pulse she could almost sense in him now. “You told me you can draw magic out of objects. That you can feel where it sits and let the orb draw it out. I’m not a scroll, but the power’s there. You can sense magic. Can you sense mine?”

Naeomi was having a hard time slipping into her trance. She willed herself to fade away. But nothing came. They were getting frustrated, unsure of why this was so difficult. She had her own room and her own bed for the first time in over a month! Then she thought about how for the past tenday her and Erthdax had been trancing next to each other. Maybe that's what was missing. They got up, grabbing a pillow from their bed and stepping out into the hallway.
Standing outside Erthdax's door, she was scared to knock. But it was either that or stand here all night. The sound was small and after a few moments passed, she was sure he wasn't going to answer. Before she could turn and scurry away though, the door opened. Looking up, she saw Erthdax, standing in a loose fitting tunic and grey lounge pants that were snug around his hips. Naeomi felt their cheeks getting warm and they swallowed.
"Naeomi? Is everything okay?" The drow asked tiredly, running his hand through his short waves. He had not yet been trancing but was certainly trying to.
The smaller elf took a few quiet deep breaths, trying to compose themself. "Ah, um, ja. Everything ist fine. I just...Ich kann nicht sleep. Can I stay here with you?"

---
“Hello. Are you one of the new members joining today?” Whitney asked, trying to be polite. The elf man sneered at him before switching to what looked more like a smile, although it looked forced.
“Ah, yes. Indeed.” The man said, his voice oddly hoarse and raspy.
With a sudden shift in tone, the man brought himself to his full height. “I saw you were all in need of a wizard, and I believe I more than exceed the needs of the role.” He loomed over Whitney with a bright gleam in his eye, making their difference in height more apparent as he looked up at the strange man.
Whitney feels the corners of his mouth tick upwards, amused by him. “May I ask your name?”
“Cornelius.”
---
Cornelius had always found himself to be the one true opposite of a people person, adverse to any and all, hateful of society and anyone who dwelled in it; he had been wronged so much in his life, so why should he give anyone a chance?
That is, until he meets a genuine, kindly werewolf, who shows him that maybe the world isn't entirely hopeless after all.
In short: Just a bunch of stories related to my DnD adjacent characters, whom I love very much :]. Enjoy!

Eirla has been through one's fair share of unusual circumstances. She has unique ways of surviving the hustle and bustle of Baldur's Gate, all while sitting on an important, life changing secret. Her profession leads her to not the finest of customers, which presents her with a big obstacle, but also a window. When the opportunity strikes, she escapes, but only to find herself in an even more unfortunate situation with even more unlikely of people.
Living a sheltered life can make one unprepared, especially in Faerun, and being lied to your whole life doesn't help. Despite her naivety, Eirla plans to use her new freedom to her advantage, but a worm to the head turns out to be the least of her issues when a mad cult threatens to take over the world.
Eirla teams with her new found friends to save Faerun, but she finds her past nipping at her heels every step of the way. Can she afford her companions discovering who she really is, or will her secrets eat away at them faster than the tadpoles?

summary:
Decades after defeating the Absolute, Astarion and Imara have settled into the life of happiness and luxury they built for themselves. Ruling their city keeps them busy and content, but when they are offered a new quest, they find themselves all too eager to be on the road and adventuring once more.
Though their quest will be long and tedious, they are determined to make the most of their time away from the burdens of leadership. summary:
“In such situations, when layer is put upon layer; when all is a façade wound within webs of deception, the truth is what you make of it.” 
Reality was malleable in the City of Glory. Like the city’s own special kind of magic.  It takes skill, practice, and commitment to obfuscate one’s self from others. To embody a role so wholly everyone around them is convinced. It is easy to get comfortable in a mask; to wear it like a real face.
Dwahvel takes great pride in her skills of observation to see through any such faces. Artemis in his powers of deception and the mask he’s managed to make for himself.

"What," Lae'zel says, "is that."
Her voice sounds severe—but then again, her voice always sounds severe, and at least there's no accompanying sound of a greatsword being drawn. Shadowheart lets her hand drop from the handle of her glaive and turns around.
"What's what?" She glances up and down the street, but there's nothing out of the ordinary to be seen: just another street in the Lower City, thrumming quietly with everyday activity. There's a pair of kids whacking each other with sticks—a steel-gray dragonborn hawking potions and dyes—a noblewoman with a stupid little purse dog, the two of them turning up their noses at a selection of vegetables—a drow wobbling on his feet, supported by friends who seem nearly as unsteady as he is—
"That." Weeks of journeying together mean that Lae'zel doesn't outright point at people anymore, but the tilt of her head is just as obvious. "That—creature."
OR: Team Tadpole plays a game. Lae'zel confronts the complexities of taxonomy.

About finally returning home in honour after breaking her back in the name of the Crying God.
Nothing will ruin this for her, not even that lascivious vampire with his mouth full of sin and a soul in need of saving.

“Avail yourself as a tool to the weary - let them know you can be used however they might need.” She blows a sharp breath out of her nose. “Sounds like a pretty clear directive to me, don’t you think?”
For once, Astarion isn’t running his mouth with a cheeky retort. When she opens her eyes, he’s staring at Salvius with a curiously intense look. She can’t imagine what might have made him so pensive, only observes that even with the world spinning, he looks very still.

It was a dream about you - all of you - and you were here with me, and I had served bread and jam and oat crackers and cheeses and enough tea to quench a desert.
You nibbled and sipped and smiled and laughed, and you asked if I was happy. Nobody has asked that for so long that I don't know if anyone has ever asked at all.
I didn't have the words to answer, so instead I led you through my House and showed you all the souls that are here with me. They were Raphael's once, but now they only belong to themselves.
The Archive is an art gallery, the boudoir is a grand kitchen, and the dungeon is a refuge for any wounded soul or creature that finds its way to us.
Am I happy? I don't know. But I am Hope, and I persist because of you.

summary:
The captain—because it must be the captain, there's no other possibility—stops directly before the straggled lines of captives. Black hair frames his angular features, the way his eyes narrow not against the sun but against them: their existence, maybe, or just the existence of all those beneath him.
There is a pause. And then he speaks.
"I am Captain Cazador Szarr of the Eternal," he says. It's a deep, almost melodic voice; too rich for the seadogs and savages that so often fill ships. Even against the better-dressed of his crew, he stands out like a noble in the East End rookeries. "And I am here to meet with your captain, pirates."The year is 1728, and Astarion Ancunín casts across the Atlantic in hopes of reaching the Caribbean to finally make a name for himself.

I rifugiati di Elturel, il peso delle scelte di Halsin, la memoria di una casa perduta: tutto si accumula come nubi basse sull’orizzonte.Alla sorgente più appartata, Kagha e Halsin si incontrano lontano dagli sguardi del Circolo. The hunger that leaves you sleepless at night, turning and tossing around in the desperate attempt to ignore the aching hollowness gnawing at your core.
Then, one day, when he finally managed to claw his way into power, he found himself surrounded by every luxury he had once only dreamed about. Fine food. Wine that cost more than whole households. Spices brought by caravans from distant shores. He enjoyed all of it.
And then, later, he met Sorrow, the beautiful, frightening creature of Bhaal, who did not understand softness and did not trust comfort.

Fünf Jahre sind vergangen, seit ihrer Flucht aus dem Norden. Diestel, die Dienerin des Pholtus, die an Ordnung glaubt. Wil Sten, der chaotische Barde, der jeden bezaubert. Manchmal sind es die eigenen Entscheidungen.Und manche Opfer haben einen Preis, den niemand zahlen sollte.Eine Geschichte über Freundschaft, Vertrauen und die Frage: Wie weit darf man gehen um ein Leben zu retten?

Post-game epilogue, in the time after Avernus when Tav, Wyll, and Karlach can take solace in a home. Their home, a cottage outside the city, a place to host their friends, their many guests, and a night of taking it all in.
----------
There was Wyll, all strength and surety at his side, and Karlach before them, a bobbing weight of pure energy.
“We’ve got it good,” Wyll said, ever the one to voice the known and the sentimental. Gods (all of them, by all the deities and hells and anything else anyone wanted to swear by), did he love his life. This thing they had found and built and molded to their scarred and dirty hands so it was something all encompassing and grand and stretching on and on so it actually had a future, and actually had roots. There was that feeling again, at the pit of him. The root of him. Something more than just drunken glee, in Tav, more than just a momentary lapse or -- he couldn’t even think of the word for it. There was a word, wasn't there? A quick euphoria? Something that’s fleeting. That’s not what it was though — no, they had endured. What they had would last.

Isobel did not know which deity or devil Ketheric had bargained with for her return to the living, but she knew with complete certainty that it had not been Selûne. The Moonmaiden had no use for the vile magic that now simmered below Isobel’s skin, closer to the Sharran weave but still not quite there. Isobel could not place the abominable power in the lifeblood that now ran through her, but she knew it was wrong.
The sickness that plagued her made her Selûnite magic slow to come, its radiant moonglow dragging slowly and painfully up the weakened veins of her arms. Her Goddess still saw her, that much she knew, but Isobel felt like she had somehow failed the Lady of Silver, had done something to cause this weakened magic.

title: Stanze del Potere
author: canesugar
tags: Dont be harsh on the lore and relationships <3
summary:
La storia di tre druide – Faldorn, Jaheira, Kagha – e il loro rapporto col potere.
Faldorn è la druida che ha scelto di rimanere – nonostante la perdita, nonostante la chiusura. Tutto ciò che ha sempre conosciuto è il terrore, interno ed esterno, che il proprio essere provava e suscitava. E’ un’umana, sola, senza scelta.
Jaheira è la druida che ha scelto la responsabilità – la sua validità pragmatica risiede nel saper catalizzare il ruolo di druida e di compagna di Khalid. Tuttavia il suo è un legame ‘bianco’, pagato a caro prezzo. E’ la pantera maculata che perde il suo colore. E’ una mezzelfa, vedova, lucida.
Kagha è la druida che ha scelto l’ombra – nella disperazione di aver perso il suo Maestro, ha trovato protezione nell’unica cosa che non era votata a lei. E’ il serpente che smette di morire e rinascere, ma rimane fossilizzato nella pietra. E’ un’elfa, abbandonata, legata.
Tutte e tre sono costrette dagli spessi viticci di spine che avviluppano le comunità druidiche – e non – di Faerun.
