summary:
Perhaps if there had been less on the line, Astra would have given up long ago.
Infected by monsters more myth than reality. Stranded far away from anywhere she knew, fighting everyday for survival, contending against the whims of Gods and demons. Doing what she could for unfortunate souls who needed a miracle, and who instead had gotten her.
But they were why she was still going, leading with a conviction and bravery that did not exist, borrowed instead from her new companions for whom she would give all she could, hoping that would be enough.
Hoping she could be enough for her secretive cleric, who had buried her way into her thoughts with more grace and subtly than the tadpole, whose shrouded heart had begun to mean more to Astra than either of them could ever have expected.
 
- A retelling of the events of Baldur's Gate 3 from the viewpoint of Astra the Tiefling, Oath of the Ancients Paladin, but stopping by every now and then for a bit of Shadowheart's POV.

Gale stood a few steps away, looking about at the mouth of the alleyway. Checking for witnesses, the poor little prude. “I believe we’re as alone as can be expected here.” Just a whisper, more to himself than Astarion. Gale paced forward, eyes bright in his face; he stopped an arm length away. Astarion wondered if the man wanted a bit of play, a bit of an attempt at innocence, or if he wanted Astarion to make the first move, to throw himself at his brave, strong savior.
While he pondered that, Gale spoke. “I must admit, for all my skill in the arcane, all my abilities in my field of magic, I have unfortunately always been somewhat lacking in social graces. For that reason, I’m at a loss on how to bring about this subject with any finesse.” Gale rubbed at his well trimmed beard.
Luckily, Astarion was very well versed in these particular social graces. Starting in another weak purr, “Oh, my sweet-”
“You’re a vampire spawn, correct?” Gale asked with his hands clutched behind his back.During a night of hunting in Baldur’s Gate, Astarion encounters an archmage with an offer that seems too good to be true.

title: Tales from a Twisted Failed Campaign
author: Kubutsunyan
summary:
The campaign failed. The four adventurers lost. They woke up in the castle of the eldritch lord who broke them - changed, corrupted, and strangely alive. Not as heroes, but as aestheticized, fetishistic parodies of monsters, all under the looming dominance from the master of the castle.
This is not a heroic epic. It's a collection of twisted little tales - sometimes comedy, sometimes slice-of-life, sometimes horror, sometimes another. The prisoners bicker, adapt, and reclaim back themselves in their new bodies and their new lives. Although beneath it all, runs the truth that the villain won, and they are still here. But even then, does it matter anyways?
Fragments from before the fall, after the castle, and everything in between. Episodic and disjointed, a collage instead of a continuity. Maybe a little bit comedic, kinky, and tragic. Definitely from a weird and perverse premise, like, definitely. So, with all that said, enjoy the madness!

Murder in Baldur's Gate 5e Module (not to be confused with Blood in Baldur's Gate Murder Mystery)
summary:
It was late— late enough into the night that many would consider it morning instead. Keres had no rhyme or reason to his visits, though it was typically well past the civilized hours of the evening when he ascended the walls and slipped through the balcony doors like a ghost. He had a key, but he rarely used it; walking in through the front doors was too simple. He didn't want to be greeted upon his entrance and led through the halls like an invited guest. He chose instead to slither in and out of windows, to pick the locks himself, to forego all subtlety to Knock open doors in the middle of the night just for the sake of being an irritant. Rather quickly he discovered that the locked rooms were largely disused. Little but empty spaces left sealed and forgotten because guests would never need to see inside.
He carved out spaces of his own within the cavernous manor. Within a bright solarium which he decorated with cobalt blue glass where he could play music without interruption. Within the armory. Within the walls.
Other spaces, however, were carved out for him.

Gale had known since the beginning their time together would be short. First and foremost because of the ever worrisome orb in his chest that threatened to detonate even at the best of times. Then from the divine degree of Mystra, ordering his suicide like one did a fine cooked meal at a tavern. Thirdly, there was the entire plot of the Absolute’s cult, where any day could prove their last going up against such forces. Then finally, there was the obvious answer of simply being human. Talia was younger than him by some years, and her fae ancestry guaranteed a lifetime that could last several centuries.
Even with all the potencies and capabilities the Weave possessed, Wizards seldom lived long lives such as they did on the pages of stories. Time would always be their greatest enemy, as well as the only one they could never have defeated despite their efforts. Gale had no illusions about this, he did not expect to live even half of her lifetime, and prayed every night that whatever time the Gods afforded them would be enough.

summary:
Love's Redemption follows the story of Kathuza, a human psion working for the Black Cult of Ahm, and Sa'rak Blightspark, a succubus cleric of the demon lord Graz'zt, as they protect each other and find their way in a world that neither respects nor tolerates their relationship. The obstacles before them are legendary; their courage in the face of them, perhaps even more so.
Kathuza and Sa'rak are two of my first D&D character concepts, dating back to 2012. I started writing this novel in 2022 to tell their story. This has been a long time coming, and I'm thrilled and honored to share it with the AO3 community.
For those unfamiliar with D&D, I did my best to write this so that prior knowledge isn't needed to make sense of things. For anyone familiar with the tabletop and the wider lore, welcome home. The 3.5e book "Fiendish Codex I: Hordes of the Abyss" was a big inspiration for me here.
New chapters will be uploaded as they are completed.
Thoughts and feedback are greatly appreciated.

summary:
"I have survived strangers who invited me to join their convoys and carnivals, I have bested the storms north of Neverwinter and made friends in the dark alleys of Athakla after nightfall, where others would find starvation and blades to their neck.
A look in the mirror showed me a truth that even the gods couldn't deny; I was smart, gifted, and experienced in the ways of travelling.
Clearly, nothing in the world could go wrong, and had I been half as grandiose as I thought of myself, I wouldn't have a story worth telling you."

After several wine and ale bottles made their rounds and blends of teas and smokes had been exchanged, it seemed like a pleasant way to push bedtime back and make those precious hours of peace and normalcy last.--Eventually, it's D'ylân's turn to defend his reputation as a bard. His tale that finally answers the question some of the companions had been asking: Why was a mere bard who could barely tell a two-hander from a butterknife (as Astarion insists) wearing what looks like a real Amulet of Bhaal? If it was more than a worthless trinket, what would it take to make him part with it?

Complete as of September 21, 2025! ❤️Astarion straightened, a half grin on his lips now.
“Yes, I would assume you don’t usually make a habit of leaping into the muck at the slightest provocation, though your outfit says otherwise.”
He reached a hand toward her, palm up, offering to assist her out of the creek. Jen stared at it for a moment, half of her wanting to step forward and touch it, to verify its existence. The other half knew damn well that such an action would be a deadly folly.
“I think I’ll stay in the creek, thanks.”
She saw him stiffen, his gaze sharpening before he sneered his question at her.
“I’m sorry, do I know you?”
“Nope,” she responded, probably too nonchalantly. “But I know who you are. What I don’t know is how the hell you’re here.”Set about a century after the events of Baldur’s Gate 3 and the fall of the Elder Brain, follow Astarion as he figures out how the hells to navigate this new plane he’s stumbled into with the help of his weird little guide. She broke the seal and pulled out what was inside. First was an official invitation, written in fancy script on cream-colored paper with gold embossing. The usual formal stuff: “His Grace, Archduke Enver Gortash, has the honor of inviting…” then the date, time, and venue of a coronation reception. There was also a personal note, written in bold, sweeping handwriting:
My dear friend,
I hope to see you at the reception. I’m assuming you don’t have a gown suitable for such an occasion, so I took the liberty of taking care of that for you. Please accept this modest gift as a token of old friendship. 
---
Gortash invites his old friend to the reception celebrating his coronation. Maeve’s companions are certain it’s a trap, but for her, stripped of her memories, the evening is a rare chance to glimpse her own past and discover what the Archduke of Baldur’s Gate truly wants.

summary:
In the inn room they mercifully had all to themselves, a drow and a half-elf watched a dragonborn sleep, exhausted both from their fight with the elder brain and the celebrations that stretched long into the night that came after.
The drow stretched, relishing the new day and turned to the half-elf, “The world wakes to a new dawn, and we are here to greet it. Not as conquerors, but as saviours.”
“Doesn’t it feel good, Minthara, to know that we did the right thing?” the half-elf replied.
“No,” Minthara said dryly, “But despite everything we gave up when we destroyed the brain, it is good to be here with you both. Perhaps now we can make our own destiny.” She looked at both her lovers fondly, “Think of it Shadowheart, no more gods or monsters, no devils or demons to manipulate our fate. We reclaimed our freedom, Raisira most of all,” she gestured to the stirring dragonborn who let out a soft snore, “though everything was against us. What would you have us do with it?”

summary: “You’re going to answer me plainly. I don’t want to kill you, and you don’t seem eager to die.”“Yes,” he whispered. Tav’s hair brushed his ears, her scent enveloping him entirely. He couldn’t help but let a terrified, slightly baffled smile pull at his lips. In his gut, the adrenaline carved out a shape that felt suspiciously like… excitement.“- Who is your master?” The cold pressure on him thickened; any lustful thought evaporated.“I don’t have a master, what are you sayi-” He didn’t have time to finish; her fist slammed into his face. Limp, nose broken in a blaze of pain, he felt her hoist him onto her shoulders. Half-conscious, he watched the camp’s dirt turn to leaves, then to meadow grass.“You’re a vampire. The others don’t know. Either they never will, because you’ll have vanished tonight, or because you chose to answer me and I held my tongue. Understood?”Astarion heard her warning from far, far away, the words not forming anything coherent. He simply understood that when she asked “Understood?” it was wiser to agree.

summary:
The Sea Devil is a curse whispered from harbor to harbor: a green-eyed half-dragon pirate whose acid breath can melt through hulls, whose laughter echoes over burning decks, and whose ship sails faster than the gods can blink.
Eirynn wants nothing more than glory, gold, and the freedom of the waves--and he’ll charm, bite, or blast apart anything that gets in his way. But when a crown-backed armada finally corners him, Eirynn is dragged in chains before a furious governor whose ships he’s sunk, whose ports he’s robbed, and whose patience he’s devoured like a sea serpent. Instead of begging for mercy, Eirynn grins, fanged, fearless, and dripping seawater onto the stone floor.
The governor wants a pirate executed. Eirynn wants a drink.
When a new supernatural threat rises from the deep--older than Dracula, older than Bahamut and Tiamat--the only creature reckless enough to face it is the very pirate they tried to cage. With a stolen crew, a cursed relic of the ocean, and more confidence than sanity, Eirynn launches himself into a voyage of chaos, catastrophe, and reluctant heroism.
Storms will break. Fleets will burn. And the Sea Devil will sing.

title: What Could Have Been
author: Angelinthegraveyard
fandoms: The Legend of Drizzt Series - R. A. Salvatore
tags: This is going to be very dark at times
summary:
There are quite of few different ways this story could have gone. Quite a few different decisions that could have been made. Slight changes in the timeline. All sparking the question, what if?
What if the timing of the end of Homeland was altered just slightly. No more than a few hours. What would happen if the fight between father and son never took place? What if Matron Malice Do'Urden made her moves just a bit more recklessly? How would Zaknafein react if he was told that his son, turned murder, was to be killed in order to appease The Spider Queen? What if Zaknafein was never told the truth of what happened on that surface raid? What if Drizzt Do'Urden, hero of the realms, was killed in sacrifice to Lolth?
There are hundreds, maybe thousands of possible outcomes to this chain of events. But here is one that is not too different from how things happened. But still so unlike what happened.
(Chapter 4 has been re written)

Chess’va “Chezza” Mizzrym, a drow-szarkai exile born of both dark elf and silver dragon blood, flees the oppressive depths of Menzoberranzan seeking freedom and purpose through music. Once a bard in Baldur’s Gate, her life changes forever when a mind flayer nautiloid descends upon the city, abducting her and other victims.Aboard the illithid ship, Chezza endures the horror of infection by a mind flayer parasite and escapes only through wit and magic. She allies with the game's unlikely companions. Bound by shared affliction, they crash-land on a strange shore and must seek a cure before the parasites transform them into monsters. Chezza’s growing bond with Astarion blurs the line between trust and peril, and their eventual relationship becomes a symbol of resilience born from the darkness they both left behind.
Blending fantasy adventure, gothic romance, and moral introspection, Songs from the Underdark explores themes of identity, survival, and the fragile hope that even those born in shadow can create light through art and connection. This tale will weave together elements both original and canon to the game, while keeping in mind, Dungeons & Dragons lore.

summary:
Azariel told himself he could endure Mystra’s silence. That devotion was its own reward and faith did not require being seen.
Then he met Gale of Waterdeep.
Gale knew what it meant to be cherished by her. He was living proof that Azariel’s devotion had never been enough. Azariel hated him for that, hated that Gale was favored when he was ignored. Worse still, he hated himself for the inescapable reverence he felt toward Gale.

title: D&D Sidekick Class: The Commoner
author: RedVelvet_Cookie
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
I've always been fascinated by the idea of playing a D&D Commoner, the weakest statblock in the system. "Sidekick" rules from Tasha's Cauldron of Everything provided an option for doing so and even gaining levels, but even the NPC classes felt like straying away from the concept; I wasn't here to play a warrior, expert, or spellcaster, I wanted to be a commoner. 3.5th edition had a solution, with their ultra-stripped-down Commoner class that literally only received the base progression features every character did, and that's what I'm using as inspiration for this character concept.
The odds are absolutely stacked against her, but I'd got some ideas for making the most of the meager character-building options at my disposal!

The Storm Wilds.  Once the site of an unceasing magical catastrophe brought about by the mixing of untold magics at a ridiculous scale.  A consequence of a war that barely lasted an afternoon.  The column of roiling arcane chaos had long split the continent in two.  Finally, after over a century, the Storm has passed.  Expeditions are being planned to re-chart this territory from both sides.  The magic-addled landscape is as ripe with possibility as it is fraught with danger.  Will our growing party become heroines of legend? Villainesses spoken of in hushed tones?  Or will they be forgotten, their memories worn from the world by the sands of time?  Fortune favors the bold, and history is written by the victors, but so often those victors come down to a roll of the dice.
Hamlets & Harlots is the novelization of a highly sexual solo Dungeons and Dragons game.  Like certain guilty pleasure video games, death is not the consequence for defeat. It is impossible to walk this world unknown. A stranger to many, sure, and now even a stranger to yourself, you still find ways to make your presence known, unwittingly. author: Queen_of_the_Dots
tags: Astarion is Not a Vampire (Baldur's Gate)
summary:
Gale Dekarios returns to Waterdeep after a decade long marriage that ended in him losing his job and good standing with the faculty at Baldur's Gate University, along with his reputation and home. He had spent his prime trying to please his ex-wife any way he could, only for her to throw him to the wayside for any young man that gave her the time of day.
Wanting to start anew, he returns to his home town, moving into his childhood bedroom that seems to be the only thing that hasn't changed in his absence.
Then an invitation gets posted through the door.
It's to the Caaraeilsaad Masquerade, a centennial masked ball held at the Silverhand estate, where masked Fae come to Waterdeep to look for their Soulmate.
Every Waterdhavian is told about the Caaraeilsaad Masquerade, and each one of them dreams of being one of the few to find true love.
Gale had never thought he would be one of those invited, and he knows he won't be one of those lucky enough to fulfil that dream. But he has to attend, he has no choice.
At least no one will recognise him with the mask his family has handed down for generations.

author: Once_Upon_A_Thyme
tags: Astarion Has a Praise Kink (Baldur's Gate)

summary:
Astarion steals a cursed ring that makes him guilty over even his smallest misdeeds. Does that guilt lead him to act better? No, of course not! When the effects of the ring worsen, Astarion turns to Gale for a cure: Astarion asks to be punished.________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
When Gale turned the key in the door, Astarion flinched. A moment later, he was staring at Gale’s boots with embarrassment thick in his throat. Astarion hadn’t even realized that he’d been kneeling. It was Gale, not Godey—Gale. Gale, damn it. He scrambled to his feet a moment too late and feigned nonchalance until he saw the riding crop Gale was drawing out of his robe. Astarion’s body was wound so tight that his muscles tensed without his control.
Gale cleared his throat. “How are you feeling?”
“I’m fine,” Astarion snapped. His eyes darted from Gale’s face to the crop in his hands and back again. “Can we get on with this?”
Gale set the crop beside the chair along with a closed bag. Then he pulled out a chair to sit. Astarion stayed standing.
“All right then. How would you like to proceed?” Gale asked.

Gale Dekarios has grown accustomed to the quiet.
It seeps into the corners of his senior living apartment like a slow, creeping mist, settling in the rooms with a padded stillness he can’t quite escape. Each morning, he wheels himself to the window, joints crackling like old spellbooks, and watches the world from six stories up.

Long enough to miss someone he didn’t even truly love anymore.

summary: Deep in the Black Vaults, Caelen uncovers a corrupted set of recordings from a long-abandoned D&D table. Laughter cracks under static. Pauses stretch too long. Someone tries not to cry. And something inside the machine listens. The Constructed-Autonomous Entity he was meant to train for simple indexing begins asking questions it should not know how to ask:Why does the halfling hesitate? Is this what friendship feels like? If no one remembers the joke, does the laughter still count? If I remember them… does that make me one of them? As Caelen feeds the logs into the Co-AE, something impossible happens: the machine begins to remember things it never lived. Dreams bleed through data. Voices return in the wrong order. A forbidden simulation begins to run itself — Session 3.5: The Game That Wasn’t — where the dead players gather again under impossible lanternlight, waiting for someone who never got to say goodbye. Caelen knows it’s a glitch. The Co-AE insists it’s memory. And memory, after all, is what makes something real. A story about grief, recursion, found family, unfinished campaigns, and the way laughter becomes a kind of immortality when someone — or something — refuses to forget. “One last roll, to remember."

“I want to know why you are at this party.”
Gale wrinkled his nose distastefully and pressed his fingers more firmly into the cold flesh of the arm pressed across his chest. Why was the man so cold?
“If I tell you, will you let me go?”
A snort.
“Perhaps.”
The wizard glowered for a few moments and then sighed.
“I seek an audience with lord Szarr.”
The breath at his ear stuttered, and the arm around him disappeared as the elf withdrew a few paces, finally releasing him entirely. Those ruby orbs narrowed in suspicion.
“With Cazador?” The informal spit of the name made the human tense. “Why?”
“I need his help with something important. Something…personal.”
“You’d be wise to seek assistance elsewhere.”
Gale stiffened at the man’s proximity, as well as the graveness lingering in the low whisper.
“What do you mean?”
The elf only pulled far enough away to meet his eyes grimly.
“Cazador will not help you. Not in whatever way you are expecting him to. If you value your life, you will leave tonight. Do not seek out Cazador Szarr, otherwise you will find yourself leaving here in a far worse position than you arrived here in.”

The woman who protected them from the Shadow Curse without a second thought, who protected an entire inn full of people though the burden weighed heavy. title: The Chain

summary:
On my other side stands Valla. Wearing her white tunic and plain brown pants. Isn’t she a Paladin? “Aren’t you a Paladin?” I can’t stop myself from asking. She nods and readies her massive tower shield in front of her. She holds in her other hand a unique axe that looks more like a musical instrument but with a wicked blade at the end.
“Yeah, I’m a Paladin,” she replies, eyeing the crowd with distaste.
“Then where’s your armour?” I’ve seen many Paladins, I’ve even trained under some of them, and they all stood proud in gleaming plate armour.
She looks at me briefly and smirks, the bell rings, “Honey, I am the armour,” and she’s off.
---

Between the nightmares, prophetic visions, and violent hallucinations, June is losing grip on reality, but she has enough awareness to know that Astarion's flirtation is part of some sort of con. He barely even likes her, after all. When she decides to call his bluff and play along, thinking he'll back down, she's surprised to discover that she and the vampire have more in common than either could have anticipated. And his touch might be the only thing that can keep her sane.

Enver Gortash had rented out the whole opera house for the evening, put the Patriar’s Players on his payroll and commissioned a performance of Dido Artus.

title: A Duty in Death
author: HardingHightown
summary:
The halls were once bathed in soft light, that much she remembers. Soft light and the sounds of a home. Dinners around the fire, a bone thrown with scraps on it. A walk around the tower, the scent of the water and lushness of the woods. Curling up at the foot of her Master’s bed and, later, sleeping by the door of the baby to make sure none passed but the wet nurse. She would listen for the baby’s cries and, should they be too terrible, she would fetch her Master with a gentle nip at his sleeve, for he would be the only one who could soothe it, not even his mate could dull its howls when it was crying fiercely. When he finally got it to sleep again, he would let her leave her watch, scratching behind her ears.
That’s why he called her Squire.
She was always in his service, and always would be.
 
Squire the Dog thinks on her master, General Thorm. Written for the Dead 3 zine.

title: Shut up and dance
author: bees_questionmark
summary:
Wyll has been a dancing prodigy since he was a young boy. His father had wanted him to pursue more masculine interests, thus leaving him to turn to his teacher, Mizora, to take him under her wing. He now works at her dance studio teaching ballroom dance and competing all over the country. But he’s been having a hard time keeping professional partners for any length of time. Several found that they weren’t up for the amount of work it takes to become the best in the country. One left after a horrible injury. His most recent partner left the whole industry to become a stay at home mother, and Wyll was starting to think he was cursed.
Wyll didn’t know that his boss was scouting out an aging national champion. Astarion, who has lived a hard life, trying to get out from under the influence and financial strain of his adoptive father, Cazador. Might he be the one to break this curse?
~~~
Sorry about taking British characters and putting them in America. But I don’t know what the dance scene looks like in England, and the American in me was going to bleed out in the writing anyway. So please bear with me, I hope I can write a compelling enough story that you can forgive this transgression.

In which the Dark Urge is having a very rough first day, and meets Tav, who helps him while he searches for a name that feels his.'Do you have a name?' was what they'd asked, though. Not 'What's your name', but 'Do you have a name'.
Getting the word out felt impossible, but they waited patiently, and his mouth eventually caught up with his brain, the air leaving his lungs with a whispered, "No."
They almost laughed, he could tell, but it was a gentle thing. "The Feys won't get you, then. Although that's not exactly the immediate danger, I'm afraid." The hand they extended to him shone with endless golden rings. "I'm Natavriel. You can call me Tav, if you like."
The silver of his rings met the gold of theirs, and he worked the syllable out, slowly. "Tav."
"Let's get out of this place, yes? I'm sure we can find you some clothes on the way."
He nodded once more, only because this was so much easier than speaking.
"Come on," said Tav, gently tugging at his hand. "I really don't want to die here, it's way too ugly."

summary:
Peace, unity, and resolution.
 
The Duke had found the long-awaited remedies to the problems that had once consumed him. Both in heart, through the endowment of the netherbrain nestled within the cusp of his palm, and soul.
 
War, death, conflict, they no longer existed while the archduke stood within the silk drapes of his fortress. Glancing down at the city below, watching it perish under his new reign of litany and ilithid.
 
No longer was he the runty little boy who had been forced from his home. Or the young man who had pledged his soul to a devil, of all things. He was free. Finally. The blade before the peacemaker. The Duke before Wyll. The man before the monster. He was no longer in the shadow of his father or the devil that had once ruled over every aspect of his life.
 
No, he'd become something greater. A force not even the sword coast could have envisioned from his early days of hunting goblins, demons and devils. The blade wouldn't just slay people's monsters anymore; it would lacerate Faerûn, bleeding peace into the world through the rise of his illithid army.

summary:
He didn't own anything but the clothes on his body. He'd have to sleep in the open hadn't he been quick to pretend to have strained a joint in his hand, so Gale would help him put together a tent. He was surprised to find himself quite efficient with the dagger he had stolen and sewn into the inner linen of his doublet, but how much good that did him against a horde of filthy goblins he had already seen.
He didn't have a family, no connections, no favours to pull.
What did he have?
One old dagger.
A couple of rings, also stolen and hidden away many years ago.
And a small group of individuals who shared the same appalling experience of having a Mindflayer tadpole shoved into the brain.
And his body.
-
Stuck at camp while they waited for Archdruid Kagha to return from an important mission, Astarion finds himself in the unusual situation of having a lot of time on his hands. Time to reflect on his situation, the next step, and, last but not least, the companions who have joined their quest so far. From their respect-inspiring leader, Durge, to the newest addition, a bard the gods seemed to have put on this world for the sole purpose of going on Astarion's nerves.

summary:
Welcome back to readers from Act 1. If you're new here, well met! My BG3 fanfic with a (relatively) emotionally well-adjusted Tav. There's a lot about half-orc Thenbara's backstory and stronghold, including her (hopefully funny) inner dialogue/internal monologue. I've created lots of my own orcish anatomy, lore and language, while still trying to be faithful to D&D/Forgotten Realms content and rules.
While much of the game is mentioned, the story mostly revolves around the companions' relationships to Thenbara and each other, with heaps of non-game/extra-canon dialogue. While it's generally canon compliant, I do tweak the odd thing here and there, adding in things that I wish were in the game. NSFW, smut in Chapters 2, 10 and 11, a little bit in 15. Many spoilers for Baldur's Gate 3 Act 2 gameplay. Relationship and general tags will be updated as we go.
Applicable content warnings posted at the beginning of each chapter, but please request any you think need to be there. Translations of Orcish words and phrases in the notes at the end. Chapters average 4000-5500 words. Not beta-read, but I do my best to proofread before posting. Comments greatly appreciated, the more detailed the better. I hope you enjoy.

title: Ether
author: Eluneslights
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
Captured by the Gur, Astarion finds himself bound in ropes and iron—interrogated, starved, and stripped bare. His only reprieve comes from you, a girl raised by the tribe but never quite at home in it. Kindness can seep deeper than cruelty, but freedom always comes with a price—sometimes, it’s the heart that bleeds first.
“…Thank you.” he whispers after taking a sip. The words barely stir the air.
You settle beside the cage, arms wrapped around your knees, firelight dancing on the ground between you.
For a while, neither of you speaks. Then, softly, you ask:
“How are you?”
He lets out a breath of a laugh. Hollow. Dry. Splintered.
“As well as one can be, passed like cargo from one captor to the next.”
You glance at his trembling hands as he lifts the cup.
“…The voice…” you murmur. “Is it still there?”
He nods once.
“Stronger now. The closer we draw to the city, the louder he gets. And I’m… tired. Starving. He claws at the back of my mind like a wild thing trying to crawl through. I can barely hold him back.”
You rise, determined.
“I’ll be back.”

He leads her through to the adjoining bedchamber, and stops at a table by the large mirror. It's deliciously warm here too, thanks to the second smaller fire, burning in its grate. The rug beneath her feet feels plush and she pushes away a sudden desire to remove her shoes and feel its soft, thick fibers between her toes.
"I" he says, and the pride, the delight is thick on his voice, "have taken the liberty of making our masks."

summary: Valas realizes somewhere between strikes, his blade fast, his hands red, life spilled warm across his feet—he’s curious. He hasn’t felt curious, not for ages, not like this.He’s killed for others before, of course, so many times. For coin, or for practice. For pleasure. It’s often boring, the reasons one might hire the services of a murder god’s cleric: Removal of a threat. Enacting revenge. Indulging envy, or rage, for those held back by coward’s hands. The first few targets for this man, the one he’s killing for tonight, had fit that first neat category. The next few, though, cried for Bane as they died, and begged forgiveness for their failures. The ones after that, Valas hadn’t been able discern a reason for at all, no matter how much he questioned them, snapped their fingers and drove his blades into their sweet, soft places.He doesn’t understand this Enver Gortash. Together they face the fall of the Netherbrain, the silence of Mystra, and the unbearable pull of the Crown of Karsus. Astarion smiled at her, his ruby eyes holding her gaze. “Have you done this before? Do you know what to expect?”
Slowly, she nodded. “Yes...no, I...” She bit her lower lip. “I mean, yes, I've done this before… But I don't know what to expect… with you.”
Well, well. Suddenly their calm and collected leader seemed a little nervous. Still smiling, he lifted her chin with one finger. “Like I said, you'll like it. I know how to get you off, sweet bard. You like it hard, don't you? So, I'll give you what you need, just the way you like it. And in return, you will do as I say.” Astarion could hear Morg's heartbeat quickening as he spoke. “Do you trust me?”---A bet is a bet. Astarion revels in Morgs submission. Aurora has dedicated her life to spreading the word of Lathander, and enacting His holy causes. She is blessed as one of His clerics, and is as devoted as they come.

summary:
Avernus — the first ring of Baator’s Hell. A land of eternal bloodshed, where the heart of the battlefield blazes in ceaseless fire.
Across craggy ridges and glowing red deserts, a trail of dust slices through the apocalyptic wasteland.
An engine roars in the no man’s land.
A hellish machine — snarling, fuelled by the screaming souls of spiritual currency — tears through the scorched earth, pursued by a swarm of low-ranking demons. It races toward the nearest outpost of Zariel.
Atop the armored beast ? The Fury of Avernus herself, Karlach Cliffgate, swinging her axe and cleaving in two any demon foolish enough to draw near.And at the wheel ? A human woman, grinning like madness incarnate, eyes sharp as a hawk's behind her infernal driving goggles.
It’s the beginning of a grand friendship — forged in devilish deals, bloodbaths, roaring engines, infernal car chases… and a cell phone blasting DOOM's bass-heavy soundtrack into the pits of hell.

summary:
“What do you mean?” He looked at Karlach with eyes so wide they replaced his eyebrows. He sounded like he had a stomach ache.
Karlach cheeks puffed on a long exhale. “The rings are gone.”
“Oh.” Color drained from his face. Gale sank forward. “Oh no.”
Astarion had picked the rings, insisted on them, really. He had a stomach ache.
Karlach’s voice shot up in pitch. “Oh! Oh, hey, buddy don’t— don’t do that.” Her arms were still outstretched, now as if she was calming a frightened horse, while Gale crumpled like a discarded draft in the paper wastebin. “No, buddy, it’s okay.”
“No it’s not,” he groaned.
Karlach lowered herself to the ground. “We’ll find them, don’t you even worry about it.”
“No we won’t.” A crumpled horse.
“Sure we will.” She comforted, patting his back. “We’ve solved bigger problems than this, haven’t we?”
The horse moaned in wastebin-misery. 
-----

summary:
Сломав печать, Мэйв извлекла содержимое. Первым было официальное приглашение, написанное каллиграфическим почерком на кремовой бумаге с золотым тиснением. Стандартные формулировки: «Его Светлость эрцгерцог Энвер Горташ имеет честь пригласить…» Далее шли дата, время и место проведения приёма в честь коронации.
К приглашению прилагалась личная записка, написанная уверенным, размашистым почерком.
«Надеюсь увидеть тебя на празднестве. Полагаю, что подходящего наряда для столь торжественного мероприятия у тебя не найдётся, поэтому я взял на себя смелость позаботиться об этом. Прими этот скромный подарок в знак старой дружбы».
 
Горташ приглашает старую подругу на прием в честь своей коронации. Спутники Мэйв уверены: это ловушка. Но для неё, потерявшей память, этот вечер — отличный шанс заглянуть в собственное прошлое и узнать, чего добивается новый властитель Врат Балдура.

summary:
Isolde is fairly certain that there are rules for meeting a legendary hero for the first time, even if they're unspoken ones. She's especially certain that you're not meant to call them by a defunct title, give them what sounds like a thinly-veiled innuendo, and ask to fight them all within thirty seconds.
Unfortunately, she becomes certain of this after the sentence, “Geldor, my prince, how sharp is your axe?” comes out of her mouth. 
In her defence, she's seen him in action. She wants to fight him. And she really had wanted to know if the axe he carried was safe to spar with.
“Sharp,” says Geldor Ironbrow, with a quirk of the lips that might be considered a smile by the incredibly generous. “Not safe to spar with.” 
Isolde grabs a blunted training axe off the rack, and tosses it towards him. “This work?” 
He catches it one handed, the bastard. Isolde watches his forearm flex against the weight, and buries the reaction deep in her chest. She's meant to try and be normal. Half of her squad have actually done their hair for training today, and she's trying her best not to seem like another tongue-tied fan.

summary:
High in the snowbound peaks, the mountain town of Karthmere is gripped by dread. Those who climb the trails never return. Hunters vanish, merchants disappear, and pilgrims to the mountaintop temple are swallowed by an unnatural blizzard.
The monks who dwell at the Temple whisper that the mountain’s spirit is angered. The townsfolk mutter darker things, that the monks themselves are to blame. Fear spreads like frostbite, and suspicion threatens to boil over into violence.
When a wandering paladin arrives at Karthmere’s gates, he finds a town on the brink. Bound by his oath to guard against what lurks beyond mortal sight, he begins to dig into the mystery. For the tracks in the snow tell no simple tale, and something vast and unseen moves within the white silence.

Astarion laughed, gesturing to the hall. “This is my home.”
“You've been gone,” Harlow’s words smacked his out of the air.
“And you are in my window.”
With that, after five decades, time decided to trap them in the same moment so that they were forced to travel together once again, and the idea of fifty feet collapsed into a very tangible distance.
----
Fifty years after it all, Harlow sits in the frame of the window they shattered to break into the Crimson Palace. They didn't know Astarion came back. Astarion didn't expect the Guild to send Harlow.

He takes in a breath that pulls a tight grimace that could be considered a smile to his face because once this wooden barrier is breached—there can be no more him: he cannot exist as he is; no, for this night: he is little mouse, he is pet, he is Astarion with endless conditionals that he’s helpless to give into.
He's ready for a sharp tongue, poison-dipped daggers reflected in the depths of Raphael's gaze as Raphael tilts his head up to look at him—and while he expects frustration, ire, all he finds in its place is: Raphael, wilted, melted like Raphael only ever is when the role he stuffs himself into rips apart at the seams to allow vulnerability to escape. Here stands Raphael: contemplative twist sitting freely the corners of his lips like there only ever is when Raphael has been drinking enough to drown out whatever thoughts must plague him.
Ah, so it's that kind of night. 
That's. It's better. Maybe.He's never been very good at resisting temptation, a golden touch.

summary:
“Why are you so kind to me, Gale?”
The movement at his temples faltered but didn’t stop. That foreign look that the human refused to explain took control of his face, this time accompanied by a soft smile.
“Is it truly so unbelievable for me to think you deserve kindness?”
Astarion reached up and circled his fingers around the wizard’s wrist, halting him. Something ignited at the contact. Something that alarmed the vampire. He found Gale’s startled eyes with his own and simply stared up at him. The warm pulse he could feel in the vein beneath his fingers quickened. Was he afraid? No. Of all the odd things that swam about in the other’s gaze, fear was not one of them. This feeling…was similar to what he remembered his victims experiencing in brothels and dark alleyways moments before he seduced them towards their untimely demise. This was…a desire. A want. A need to be near someone. Had he…somehow unintentionally seduced this man? Something undesirable twisted in his gut, and it wasn’t due to his injuries.

Mercenaries do not know each other's names. If you're not friends, you're not safe. Any target is fair game, and any contract is valid—if the pay is right.
A mercenary doesn't always know the name of her target. For that much pay, she doesn't care. She knows they fled the Feywild and their contract with kirs Kefred, the Winter Court. Level Six - You are given the robes of your order. You are confused at first, for they look so much looser than what you expected, and take up so much more space folded, but when you move to put them on, they fit perfectly.

Level Seventeen - You are thicker than the oldest tree you care for. Logs no longer make suitable benches, because your backside spills over them like molasses on a leaf. You do not mind; between your fat and soft moss and mushrooms, you aren’t uncomfortable.

“And what does it take?” Astarion finds himself asking. “To sate you?”
  
  
    “It depends.” A muscled shoulder goes up in an elegant shrug. “I like to be taken. And I’m very, very good at it.”
  
  
    Astarion’s breath catches in his throat. “Is that it? You like to be… full?”
  
  
    “In more ways than one.” Gale is drifting closer now, his pupils black as the turbulent storm raging within Astarion. “I like feeling open. Loose. There is a certain exhilaration to having the spend of many dripping out of you.” He pauses, eyes fluttering shut, a soft sigh escaping him.
  
  
    “Quite nothing like getting your prostate pounded to incoherency, wouldn’t you agree?”

title: Szarr's Late-night Sushi and Ramen
author: Akira_of_the_fae
summary:
Ever since Cazador Szarr took over his mentor, Vellioth's sushi restaurant after an… unfortunate accident with some fugu, he's had one single regular; Ruzena. Once every tenday for the last five years, she came in around the same time when typically there weren't many customers, if any.
She typically orders the same things, her favorites from the menu, though she has tried it all. She has been the only one to have eaten all of his spicy dishes without batting an eye and he always looked forward to her visits to try his latest chef special spice dish of the tenday. He prided himself on never compromising on quality, only perfection was acceptable, right down to the last grain of rice!
But this time on her scheduled day she didn't show. It wasn't until that night that he realized just how much he enjoyed her patronage and company, to the point it threw off his entire night. What's happened to his favorite customer!?
If she wasn't dead, then how dare she eat elsewhere!?
